title: Ask ERP manual
text: Plain-words notes for people who use the ERP. Ask ERP reads this file, the glossary and the posting patterns when it answers. If an answer is wrong or missing, fix it in the document it came from.

title: What Ask ERP is
text: Ask ERP answers questions about how the ERP works and about the company's own figures. It answers only from the approved documents and from the screens you are allowed to see. It cannot change anything. It does not show pay, ID numbers or private logins. If it does not know, it says so. Ask one store and one period at a time for the best answers. Questions may be in English or Taglish.

title: Who sees what
text: Each person sees only the stores they are assigned to, and only the screens their role allows. A manager sees the reports for their own stores. Staff see their own screens. If Ask ERP says it cannot show something, the same screen is closed to you in the ERP: ask an admin if you think you need it. An admin can open a screen for one person, or for a whole position under Position access defaults (/admin/access-defaults).

title: Recording an expense
text: Open Expenses, then New expense (/expenses/new). Choose the store, the date, the supplier and the category, then the amount. An expense that is a bill to pay later is booked to accounts payable. An expense paid by a staff member out of their own pocket is a reimbursement (/expenses/reimbursements). Bills that repeat every month are set up under Recurring expenses (/expenses/recurring) and drafted for you. A budget cap on a category only warns; it never blocks an expense.

title: Cash requests
text: A cash request (/cash-requests) is money given out ahead of a purchase. It must be liquidated afterwards: the receipts are recorded and any change is returned. A cash request not liquidated for a long time shows up in Findings.

title: Suppliers and bills
text: Suppliers are under Accounts payable (/ap/suppliers). The bills still owed are on /ap. Everything the company still owes in one place (bills, loans, other obligations) is on /liabilities/unpaid. Wages are not part of what Ask ERP shows.

title: Reading the money: reports
text:
- Income Statement (/reports/income-statement): sales, cost of sales, expenses and profit for the dates you pick, for one store or all of yours. - Store Comparison (/reports/store-comparison): the income statement of several stores side by side. - Sales Rollup (/reports/sales-rollup): sales by day, month or store, and by channel (walk-in, Grab, Foodpanda). - Spending by Item (/reports/expense-items): where the expense money went, by group, category and item. This is the report to ask about cost drivers. - Balance Sheet, Cash Flow, Trial Balance, AP Aging and AR Aging are under Reports too. - Budgets (/budgets): the cap per category per period against what was actually spent.
A figure always belongs to a period and a store. When Ask ERP gives a figure it names both.

title: Stock
text: Stock on hand and the moves are under Inventory (/inventory). Low stock (/inventory/low-stock) lists the items at or below their threshold, worst shortage first. An item with no threshold set does not appear there; it shows as a finding so a manager sets one. Physical counts are at /inventory/counts and moves between rooms or stores at /inventory/transfers.

title: Cash, till and remittance
text: The till and its counts are at /till. Cash kept at a store that must be handed over to the office is tracked under Remittance (/remittance). A counted shortage on a closed shift is a finding until someone resolves it.

title: Sales days
text: Each store's sales for a day are recorded and verified under Sales days (/sales-days). A sales day that was changed after it was verified is flagged.

title: Findings
text: Findings (/findings) is the list of things the system noticed: books that do not tie, cash not remitted on time, unusual spending, a store with items that have no reorder threshold, and more. Unusual spending is checked per store: a category far above its usual week, one expense far above its usual, many more expenses than usual, a possible duplicate, an expense approved by the person who recorded it, and spending over a budget cap. These only warn; nothing is blocked. A finding stays on the list while it is still true. Accepting a finding for a while does not make it disappear from the count.

title: People and attendance
text: Staff, attendance and payroll have their own screens (/staff, /attendance, /payroll). Pay and personal details are private and are not available through Ask ERP.

title: Settings
text: Stores, access, business rules and the AI hub are under Settings (/settings). Only a super admin can use the AI hub, which holds the AI keys and the monthly spending cap. The number of questions one person may ask a day is also set there.

title: Glossary — what the words actually mean
text:
Living document. This exists because in this domain the obvious reading of a name is often wrong, and an agent that guesses writes confidently incorrect code. Add an entry the moment a term surprises you. That is the trigger — not "is this important", but "did I have to go read code to find out what this meant".
- The name lies. The obvious reading is wrong. Read before using
- Verified in code on the cited line
- Business usage, from Ian — not a code artefact
---

title: dineInSales
text:
Means: unlimited-package sales only. *Not* "all dine-in".
À la carte and online both fall into walkIn. ERP does not compute this field — it pulls it from POS. Consequence: it maps straight to account 4100 (dine-in, unlimited) with no reconstruction needed.

title: takeOutSales
text: A residual, not a measurement. Math.max(0, totalGross - dineInSales) (POS/src/app/api/external/sales/route.ts:53). It absorbs everything totalGross counts that dineInSales does not — today that is à la carte only, because no online orders exist yet. Never treat it as a revenue figure on its own; treat a non-zero value as a reconciliation signal.

title: dineInSales — ALSO means something different in the ERP than in POS
text: The entry above defines POS's meaning (unlimited-package sales). The ERP's sales-report form stores something else in the same field: *"Stored dineInSales — the remitted-daily channels"* (derive-totals.ts:83-85). One field name, two meanings, depending on which system wrote the row. Anything reconciling ERP against POS must know which it is holding.

title: cashPayments — a floored residual, not a measurement
text: *"cash is DERIVED: remitted channels − online − credit − other, floored at 0"* (derive-totals.ts). Flooring at zero hides a negative, and a negative here would be a real signal that the tender figures disagree. Same family as takeOutSales: a residual wearing a measurement's name.

title: sessionMode
text: Two values only: 'package_dinein' | 'alacarte'. Walk-in à la carte and in-store take-out are the same value — there is no take-out flag anywhere in POS. Online orders live in a separate onlineOrders collection and get sessionMode: 'alacarte' hardcoded onto a synthesised receipt. See .

title: session
text: A group of diners at a table, from seating to payment. Not an auth session, not an HTTP session. When you mean authentication, say *auth session* explicitly.

title: attendance day
text:
The adjudicated result for one person on one shift day — hours, breaks, night differential, anomalies.
Never called a "session". session above already means *a group of diners at a table*, and packages/db/schema/sessions.ts already took the second meaning for auth. v1's attendanceSessions would be the third meaning of one word in one system.

title: Sales and service
text:
unli / unlimited / package - The core product: unlimited samgyupsal, fixed price per head, variable consumption. Its margin moves with *how much people eat*, which is why it gets its own revenue account (4100)
à la carte - Ordering individual items rather than the package. Sold both dine-in and take-out
take-out - Always items / à la carte — never unli. Includes delivery: *delivery is a mode of take-out, not a third channel*
refill - A repeat serving within an unli session. Cooldown 60s, anchored on SERVE not order, with two safety valves (10 min "still in kitchen", 20 min "first serving pending"). All magic numbers in app code today —
addon - An extra item bought during a package session. Counted into dineInSales via dineInAddonSalesAmount
kitchen ticket - The kitchen's copy of an order. billOnServe: true means no bill line exists yet
billOnServe - The bill is created on SERVE, not on order. Recognise revenue at order instead and unserved orders become revenue. POS/src/lib/kitchen/customer-order-billing.ts
void - Cancels the *sale*. In POS a void is a status flip on the same document, not a reversing entry

title: Sales and service (cont.)
text:
refund - A separate negative receipt referencing a parent. Currently mints colliding numbers —
re-ring - A corrected receipt replacing a voided one; consumes the retained void cash
voidCashRetained - Cash collected on a voided receipt and not refunded. It sits in the drawer backing no sale, so ERP carries it into expected remittance and books it to a suspense liability
comps - Complimentary items. Contra-revenue (4950), confirmed by Ian — not marketing expense
day feed (T-375) - The stored, immutable copy of one POS v1 response for one store-day (pos_v1_day_feeds): the exact text, its parsed form and a sha256. A sales day on a linked store is DERIVED from it and nothing else. Append-only: every fetch is a fact, none is edited or de-duplicated. Interim — retired per store at P2, when that store's sales reach Postgres directly (ADR-015)
linked store (T-375) - A store with a row in pos_v1_store_links. That row is the whole switch — no flag, no env var. Linked: its sales days are imported from POS and never typed. Unlinked: today's typed path, labelled "Typed — store not linked to POS"

title: Sales and service (cont.)
text:
unlinked store (T-382) - A store whose pos_v1_store_links row has unlinked_at set. It takes typed sales days again; days already imported from POS stay as they are (verified ones frozen by the 0185 lock, hardened by 0187). Its row keeps its POS id, so no other store can link that POS store. An admin can relink it (an UPDATE of the same row). "Linked" means a LIVE row
tender (master) (T-375) - A store's tender definition (tenders): a name, cash or wallet, the money account a wallet pays into, and how POS v1 spells it. Not sales_day_tenders, which is one day's wallet rows (where that day's money went). The master is what a till will sell against; sales_day_tenders is what a day recorded
payment option (T-629) - One of the ORG's master list (payment_options): Cash, GCash, Maya, QRPH, Credit card, Debit card. It owns the NAME and the KIND (cash or wallet). A store switches it on by holding a tenders row for it (so a tender IS the store's switch); tenders.name / tenders.kind are a mirror a trigger keeps equal to the option. Group company-wide by payment_option_id, never by tender name

title: Sales and service (cont.)
text:
platform sales (T-375) - Foodpanda, Grab and similar: typed per day on the store's NON-remitted channels, kept outside the figures POS derives. One removable seam, until platforms are rung through POS
wholesale (item flag) (T-443) - items.sellable_wholesale. Not "sold in bulk": it means the item may be sold to another store, a franchisee or an outside buyer (e.g. Xlice) — anyone who is not a diner. The commonest case is the commissary (Lipa) selling to the company's own branches. The word is kept in code and in soldAsLabel; screens say "Sold to other stores or buyers (wholesale)". v1 called the own-branch case commissary → branch sales (computeBranchPrice)
variation (item) (T-443) - An item grouped under a top-level parent through items.variant_of_item_id (Kimchi 250g under Kimchi). Each variation is a full item — own code, stock, price history — not a pack size of one pool (Ian, R-A). One level only; a variation has the same kind as its parent. Not purchase_unit (a buying container) and not parent_slab_item_id (slab to slices) and not menu_item_variants (the MENU side)

title: Sales and service (cont.)
text: store charge / charge_total / amountDue (T-627) - An extra peso amount a cashier adds to a bill for things outside the menu (leftover food, an extra griller). Not a service charge (none is charged) and not part of total: charges come AFTER discounts and VAT, outside the VAT base, never discounted, never in the senior/PWD base. On a receipt total = subtotal - discount_total still holds; charge_total sits beside it and amountDue (priceSession) = total + charge_total is what the customer pays. pos_day_closes.gross_total and the Z's grossTotal are what was BILLED (total + charges); the sales day books them as other_charges (4500), never service_charge

title: Sales and service (cont.)
text:
reservation deposit / deposit_applied / deposits_applied / account 2170 (T-628) - Money a customer paid ahead to hold a table. Not sales and not income when taken: it is a liability (2170 Customer deposits payable) until it is applied to the bill, refunded or kept by a manager (then 4500). Its balance is derived from the append-only events (taken - voided - applied - refunded - kept), never stored. pos_sales_receipts.deposit_applied is the part of a bill paid from it (a payment line "Deposit", not a tender row); sales_days.deposits_applied is the Z total, posted Dr 2170 by routeSalesDay as a tender of the sale. Taken / voided / refunded / kept post beside the Z of the till that moved the cash (pos_deposit entries), so the drawer matches the day the cash moved. A void is refused once applied; a cancelled or no-show reservation with money held cannot close until a manager refunds or keeps it, with a reason
refunds (sales day) (T-375) - sales_days.refunds: POS refunds of the day, contra-revenue 4950, on a feed-sourced day only. Never comps — comps keep their meaning (complimentary items). Derived as the amount by which POS's method totals exceed its paid total, above the rounding band

title: Money and books (cont.)
text:
normal balance - Whether an account naturally carries a debit or credit. A declared column in v2 — never inferred from a code prefix, which is how the legacy system got it wrong
fiscal period - A dated window with status open / closed / locked. No posting into a closed period by any ordinary path, including crons and ETL. The one way in is the admin override (bible row 193): admin and super_admin only, a typed reason, an audit row, and the exemption dies with the transaction. The period stays closed; reopening is still not built
trial balance - The one-query check that total debits equal total credits. Must pass at any moment
legacy_code - The old system's account identifier, kept on the new account so migrated data can be traced back
management ledger - What this system is. Not a statutory filing basis. VAT here is a label; reported sales are not all sales. Never label or export output as BIR-ready — bible §13 row 75

title: Money and books (cont.)
text:
owed (remittance) - What a store's cashier drawer still has to hand over for one date: that date's cashier-cash movement (journal lines on 1110-1130 held by the cashier) minus what posted remittances already allocated to it. Derived on read in repo/remittance.ts, never stored. A date can owe money whether or not anyone has verified its sales day
remittable - Not "this money may be remitted." It is sales_days.status = 'verified' for that date (repo/remittance.ts:99): a statement about the sales day, not about the cash. A day that is not remittable can be holding real cash in the drawer right now, and the remittance screen shows that cash anyway
settleable - A date a handover can be applied to: remittable and owed > 0. createRemittance allocates oldest-first across settleable dates only, and refuses before any write when there are none
variance (remittance) - Signed. Handed over minus what the settleable days owed: negative is short, positive is over, zero is an exact match (remittance/allocate.ts). varianceDayId says where the arithmetic put the difference (the last day that owed anything), never who caused it

title: Money and books (cont.)
text:
float (till) - money_accounts.float_target: the amount a cashier drawer is meant to keep (at most one per store). At a float store a handover carries only what the verified days owe, and the float stays in the drawer; extra float goes back to the office as a transfer
overdraft (money account) - An outflow that would take an account below zero. A property of the account, not the feature (bible rows 154, 161): a cashier drawer is warned and still posts (its sales are not in the books until verify), down to a per-account cap admin sets; an office or staff account is refused

title: Slicer pay (T-635)
text:
performed_by_person_id - who sliced a slice record; NOT created_by (whoever typed it) or posted_by
confirmed_by_person_id / confirmed_at - another staff member checked the slicing; never the slicer; cleared by an edit
is_paid (production line) - an OUTPUT line the slicer is paid per kg for; false = re-cut or trimming
paid_by_pay_run_id (production record) - the posted pay run that paid it; set on post, cleared on void; while set the record cannot be edited or voided
slicer_pay (payslip) - per-kg pay in gross, NOT in basic_pay
worked_as (punch / day / adjustment) - regular or slicer. The punch carries what the person chose at clock-in (null = no choice = regular); the day's value is DERIVED on every recompute (first clock-in, or a live worked_as adjustment); a slicer day pays 0 from the daily rate
isSlicer (roster mirror document) - the offline kiosk asks only these people "Working today as: Slicer / Regular staff"
slicer_days / slicer_earlier_records (payslip) - days paid as slicer days (days_worked is the REGULAR days); records paid that were confirmed late, from before the period

title: Words we deliberately avoid
text:
"v1" for this project - legacy ERP / Shareat System - "v1" means the legacy ERP in ~170 places. This project has no version number
"dine-in" for a metric - name the account — 4100 unli, 4150 à la carte - "dine-in" is ambiguous exactly where it matters
"sync" between apps - publish (Lane A) or ingest (Lane B) - "Sync" implies bidirectional. Nothing here is bidirectional
"the API" - name the app and route - Four apps had eight cross-app routes. Ambiguity here caused real bugs

text: SUPERSEDES #17. Parity splits three ways: workflow FIXED, accounting NOT parity, data handling FREE (§1.3) Why: Golden-mastering accounting against v1 would certify v1's defects as v2's requirements

title: Decision 25 (2026-08-22)
text: Accounting oracle is double-entry law, not v1; divergences logged in ACCOUNTING-DIVERGENCES.md (§16.2) Why: v1 is a comparison subject, not a target

title: Decision 26 (2026-08-22)
text: Target is the midpoint: correct like ERPNext, simple for one business (§16.4) Why: Ian: ERPNext's structure is superb but overkill; the business is not an empire

title: Decision 28 (2026-08-22)
text: Phases resequenced: accounting spine 4→1, attendance 2→4 Why: Everything posts into the ledger; attendance risk retired by a Phase-0 spike instead

title: Decision 29 (2026-08-22)
text: The ETL doubles as an audit of v1's books (§1.4) Why: A schema with real constraints rejects exactly the entries that are wrong

title: Decision 30 (2026-08-22)
text: PH statutory rates are effective-dated data in one module, never inline constants (§16.5) Why: Historical runs must reproduce their original figures

title: Decision 32 (2026-08-22)
text: Invariants go from nine to ten: nominal ledger and control accounts split out Why: Discovery showed v1 lacks both entirely

title: Decision 33 (2026-08-22)
text: Minimum two lines per journal entry, enforced by CHECK constraint; no single-leg escape hatch Why: balancer.ts:64-67 is the hole everything leaked through

title: Decision 34 (2026-08-22)
text: §16.7 known-defect table is the acceptance criteria for Phases 1–3, not a wish list Why: Turns diagnosis into testable requirements

title: Decision 37 (2026-08-22)
text: Account lifecycle active / reserved / archived (§16.9) — nice-to-haves are reserved, not active Why: Keeps everything without the miscoding and report-noise cost of unused active accounts

title: Decision 38 (2026-08-22)
text: Per-counterparty GL accounts become control account + subledger Why: v1 has one GL account per supplier/customer; no independent check on the total

title: Decision 39 (2026-08-22)
text: normal_balance is a declared column, never inferred from an account-name prefix Why: v1's inference silently defaults to debit for any unlisted prefix

title: Decision 40 (2026-08-22)
text: POSTING-PATTERNS.md — one canonical pattern per business event — is a Phase 1 deliverable (§16.10) Why: Aligning accounts without aligning entries still yields wrong books

title: Decision 41 (2026-08-22)
text: Inter-store reciprocals must eliminate to zero (invariant 6) Why: Makes the cross-store transfer verifiable rather than best-effort

title: Decision 42 (2026-08-22)
text: staff_reimbursable is a LIABILITY (2130) — Ian: "we owe to staff, staff own money they spend for business needs" Why: Confirms a live misclassification: it sits on the asset side today because nature defaults to debit

title: Decision 43 (2026-08-22)
text: Revenue splits dine-in unli / dine-in à la carte / take-out; delivery is a mode of take-out, not a channel. Beverage splits alcoholic / non-alcoholic Why: Ian's actual sales model. Unli is a different economic product — fixed price, variable consumption — and its margin is the key business signal

title: Decision 44 (2026-08-22)
text: channel_id added as a second dimension (nullable, revenue and channel-fee lines only). AMENDS §16.4 Why: Per-channel P&L without multiplying revenue accounts; platform fees differ per channel

title: Decision 45 (2026-08-22)
text: Points and vouchers are contra-revenue, not tender. Voucher accounts reserved; 2145 Unredeemed vouchers reserved for a future sold-voucher model Why: Ian: earned and redeemed as discount; selling is a maybe, later

title: Decision 46 (2026-08-22)
text: Payroll moves to standard accrual with a draft pay run. Expense + employer contributions posted on approval; payout clears the liability. Cash out before approval is an advance (1235) Why: v1 parks gross against a liability that then carries a debit balance. The 3-day settle is a draft-state problem, not an accounting-model problem — and Ian wants the system to shorten that cycle

title: Decision 47 (2026-08-22)
text: expensetax → 6800 Taxes and licences; permits are non-VAT-able so no input VAT Why: Ian: mostly permits

title: Decision 48 (2026-08-22)
text: loss_on_disposal → 7400, on the P&L Why: Ian: yes. Write-offs have never reduced reported net income

title: Decision 49 (2026-08-22)
text: Statutory obligations get a subledger, aging report, and a dashboard tile beside cash (§16.5) Why: Ian asked how unremitted SSS/PhilHealth/Pag-IBIG would be tracked. v1 books none of it, so the obligation exists in law but nowhere in the books — unremitted withholding looks like free cash

title: Decision 50 (2026-08-22)
text: COGS categories map to an (inventory account, COGS account) pair, not one expense account Why: Purchase and consumption are different events; this is what puts stock on the balance sheet

title: Decision 51 (2026-08-22)
text: Interest expense and loss on disposal reclassified out of OPEX into other income/expense Why: They are not operating costs; improves comparability of operating margin. Net income unchanged

title: Decision 52 (2026-08-22)
text: Catch-all categories are kept but their share of spend is reported Why: Forcing spend into wrong-but-specific categories is worse; the fix is visibility, not removal

title: Decision 53 (2026-08-22)
text: The four verbs — duplicate what's good, correct what's wrong, add what's missing, delete what's not needed and redundant (§1.2) Why: Ian's standing rule. Relaxes strict workflow parity: v2 is not a pixel-copy of v1

text: Skills are lenses, not assurance (§15.12). Use accounting-systems; never install an unvetted skill as a correctness control Why: A skill cannot catch a wrong number; only a test can. False confidence is worse than none

text: accounting-systems is invoked before writing any posting pattern Why: It independently confirmed the staff-reimbursement liability call and added 10 rules we had missed

title: Decision 60 (2026-08-22)
text: Adopted from the skill: single period-assignment rule, single aging basis, no unallocated payments, duplicate-invoice detection, WHT at posting, variance to suspense, void≠reverse, 3-stage cash-advance lifecycle Why: Standard controller practice

title: Decision 63 (2026-08-22)
text: ERP availability requirement is lower than assumed — POS and the customer app are independent, so ERP downtime costs back-office time, not revenue Why: Argues against over-engineering HA. Does not relax durability

title: Decision 65 (2026-08-22)
text: PostgreSQL forbids DEFERRABLE on CHECK constraints. Balance + minimum-two-lines must be a CONSTRAINT TRIGGER ... DEFERRABLE INITIALLY DEFERRED; per-row rules stay immediate CHECKs Why: Balance is inherently multi-row — an entry is legitimately unbalanced after its first line and need only be correct at COMMIT. Caught by the walking-skeleton test before Phase 1 was built on it

text: Money crosses the wire as a string, computed in integer centavos; moneyFromLegacyFloat() is the ETL-only escape hatch and flags every ambiguous source value Why: Reproduce v1's figure, surface the doubt (§11 rule 5)

title: Decision 77 (2026-08-23)
text: Offline scope is CLOSED: POS selling + ERP biometric/attendance clock. Nothing else. Availability tolerance is 10 minutes to 1 hour superseded in part by row 276: POS tolerance is now 24 hours, per device; the scope (POS + clock) still holds Why: Ian, asked directly: those are the only two offline needs, and an outage of 10 minutes up to an hour is workable. This is a major simplification. CUSTOMER and the Website become online-only. POS does not need a local database per store or bidirectional sync — the two-lane Firestore model already designed in §5 is sufficient, because a one-hour tolerance turns offline from a correctness problem into a queue-and-replay problem. The remaining hard case is receipt numbering while offline, which needs its own design (pre-allocated blocks or device-prefixed sequences reconciled on reconnect)

title: Decision 78 (2026-08-23)
text: Integration plumbing between apps is DELETED, not migrated. But its business rules are harvested first Why: Ian: drop all the mapping that exists only to let the apps talk to each other. Correct — with one backend, the api/external/* routes, external API keys and key-scoping, the POS→ERP sales pull and its field mapping, the payment-method mapping layer, the storefront-catalog feed, and the cross-app idempotency/dedup maps all become dead weight. They are workarounds for separation, and separation is gone. The hard caveat: that code also encodes business semantics learned the expensive way — void-cash-retained disposition, branch-sale reconciliation, payment-method classification, refill timer anchoring. Deleting the plumbing is right; losing the rules inside it is not. Discovery docs 09–12 and CROSS-APP-MAP.md exist to harvest them BEFORE anything is deleted. Two things that are NOT app-to-app linking and must survive: the Lane A/B Firestore edge cache (offline, §5 + row 77) and the historical ETL mapping (T-113 — history was recorded in the old shape and still has to load)

title: Decision 84 (2026-08-23)
text: The reference repos are read as REQUIREMENTS, not as design. Intent is authoritative; implementation is not (§1.2b) Why: Ian: *"whatever you discover there is made by me, not 100% sure correct... but the intent I put is always there. I made features there because we use it in day-to-day operations. Implementation might be flawed but get the idea, refine it to correct execution."* v1 is the most detailed statement of WHAT this business needs that exists anywhere — more complete than any spec, because the person who runs the business wrote it for the business he runs. This closes the gap between §1.3 (workflow is fixed) and §2 rule 1 (read-only): an agent must neither dismiss a feature because its code is poor, nor faithfully reproduce a flaw because "v1 is the oracle". A feature that looks pointless is a signal to ask, never to delete

title: Decision 85 (2026-08-23)
text: etl/ moves under packages/etl/ as @shareat/etl — a real workspace package, not a bare scripts folder. T-117's replay-harness corpus, taxonomy, pseudonymisation and converter live there Why: Task spec docs/tasks/117-replay-harness-stage-a.md explicitly named this move in its Scope ("PROJECT_BIBLE.md §8 (layout — etl/ becomes packages/etl/)"). Making it a package (not etl/ at repo root, which §8 previously described) means it is unit-tested by the same packages//*.test.ts convention every other package uses, covered by the app-boundary test (tests/unit/app-boundaries.test.ts, which already scans all of packages/), and consumable by name (@shareat/etl) if a future app or script needs its converter/taxonomy. packages/* already matched it via the existing workspace glob — no package.json change was needed. The pre-existing empty top-level etl/ directory is superseded and left in place, untouched, rather than deleted (out of this task's scope)

title: Decision 86 (2026-08-23)
text: A task spec may NEVER authorise an implementer to amend this bible. Row 85 was written by a Sonnet implementer because T-117's spec listed PROJECT_BIBLE.md in its allowed Scope Why: §14 is explicit: *"Who may amend: Opus, in planner role. A Sonnet implementer never amends it — it reports a conflict and stops."* My spec granted a permission the bible forbids, and §14's own conflict rule (bible > task spec) means the spec could not grant it. The content of row 85 is correct and is kept; the process was wrong. Correct pattern: the implementer reports the amendment it believes is needed, and the planner makes it. A spec that lists the bible in Scope is a defect in the spec

title: Decision 88 (2026-08-23)
text: The Flutter handheld inventory app is DROPPED — not ported Why: Ian: *"no, I dropped it."* Its eight authenticated routes (/api/inventory/*, /api/meat/adjust, /api/production/*, /api/deliveries/*) are dead code in the legacy system. A DELETE under §1.2, and correctly Ian's call because it removes a user-facing capability. Do not resurrect these routes when porting the inventory domain — their presence in v1 is not evidence of a need

title: Decision 89 (2026-08-23)
text: Smart-reorder is revived as a deferred ADD, not a Phase 1/2 concern Why: Ian: *"revive, but later."* Real functionality (14-day projection, seasonality, AI recommendations, alerts dashboard) that existed and was removed, leaving debris: archive/TODO-smart-reorder.md stamped DONE, firestore.rules still guarding a deleted reorder.actions.ts, vestigial reorderPoint/reorderQuantity on the item form. Nice-to-have under row 87

title: Decision 91 (2026-08-23)
text: Phase plan revised: every one of the 33 unowned capabilities now has a phase (docs/CAPABILITY-GAPS.md) Why: Phase 2 gains the five ledger-posting financial modules it silently omitted, which expands the January cutover scope. Phase 3 gains the commissary→branch pipeline as a named deliverable — ~24 capabilities that straddled Phases 2 and 3 and were owned by neither, which is exactly how a branch store's entire replenishment path went unplanned. Staff master record and position taxonomy move to Phase 4 as explicit prerequisites of 4 and 5. Nice-to-haves are deferred, not unassigned — row 87's distinction

title: Decision 93 (2026-08-23)
text: Model selection is a deliberate choice per task, not a default (§3.1a): Sonnet explores and implements, Opus plans and reviews, Fable is reserved for two specific cases Why: Ian: *"juggle Fable, Opus and Sonnet for the specific task that needs them."* Sonnet is the default for delegated work — code reading, discovery, capability inventories, executing a written spec. Opus owns planning, architecture, specs, review, and anything landing in §13. Fable is reserved for (1) a bug that has already survived a deliberate Opus pass, and (2) genuinely intricate data-shape design where getting the shape wrong is expensive to undo. Two guards recorded with it: "Opus found it hard" is not the bar for escalation — a systematic pass must have been made and failed — and Opus must not be spent on what Sonnet does well, because every Opus turn on mechanical reading is a decision not being made

title: Decision 100 (2026-08-23)
text: ADR-006 — period close: month is a pure lock, year posts exactly one entry into 3300 Retained earnings Why: First real use of §3.6 (research before planning), and it paid: the research found no consensus even among the reference systems, and Odoo's *actual* stated reason for reversing its position in v19 (audit-trail commingling), which corrects an earlier hedge. Month close posts nothing — invariants 2/3 already make a month-range P&L a live query, so the existing trigger is the whole mechanism. Year close calls the existing postEntry, correctable by the existing reverseEntry. No closing-voucher entity: ERPNext's PCV and Tryton's wizard exist to provide a submit/cancel/amend lifecycle around a closing entry, and we already built that generally for every entry. Requirement, not detail: the year-close entry must carry a distinct source_type so a date-range P&L can exclude it while a balance-sheet-as-of includes it — GnuCash's docs concede its identical feature breaks its own reports for exactly this reason. Subledger tie-out is a HARD gate from year one, against the research's softer suggestion: low volume makes the gate cheap to satisfy, not burdensome, and a gate introduced once volume is high is the one that gets bypassed

title: Decision 101 (2026-08-23)
text: Close calendar: a closed year is NEVER reopened, and the year closes 15 JANUARY — December carries a 15-day correction window (ADR-006 §7) Why: Ian. The holidays are the busiest and messiest trading period and the books need time to settle. The window is what makes never-reopen fair — they are complements, not a compromise: never-reopen with a same-day close would be brutal. And it is standard practice — no real operation closes a period on the day it ends. Three obligations follow: 15 Jan must be treated as hard (a window's value is that it closes; slip once and it slips every year) — revised from 31 Jan the same day; the shorter hard window is the better one, ~10 working days after the New Year holiday, and the binding constraint is whether supplier invoices arrive rather than the window length; December figures are provisional for a fortnight and reports MUST say so; and the window must be used, not consumed in the last three days. Month close IS enforced — revised same day, see row 103. Admin and manager may close. closed → locked auto-advances once the next year's close posts

title: Decision 102 (2026-08-23)
text: ~~No monthly close is recommended — the reasoning is the OPPOSITE of the intuition. A soft "reviewed" marker is recommended instead Why: Asked directly. Months staying open is MORE accurate, not less: an error found in November dated March posts to March, where it belongs. Hard-closing would push it into November — freezing March but polluting an unrelated month, which makes a March-vs-April comparison *worse*, not better. For internal management analysis, accuracy-by-period beats stability of the reported number. The genuine cost of never closing is accountability, not accuracy: a month reviewed, acted on, then changed leaves the decision resting on a number that no longer exists. A soft marker fixes exactly that — month marked reviewed with who and when, postings still legal but flagged, analytics showing provisional vs reviewed. The review is the monthly discipline; the lock never was~~ — SUPERSEDED SAME DAY BY ROW 103. My recommendation was wrong; kept because the reasoning trail matters

title: Decision 103 (2026-08-23)
text: Months close too. EVERY period — month and year — closes on the 15th of the following month. One rule, no exceptions (ADR-006 §7.3) Why: Ian, reversing his own §7.3 answer and overruling my row-102 recommendation. He is right and I was wrong, for a nameable reason: my argument was frequency-blind. The cost I emphasised (a November-found, March-dated error landing in November) is rare — daily POS reconciliation surfaces most errors inside 15 days. The benefit (monthly figures that stop moving) is used every month. I weighed a rare cost against a constant benefit and got the trade backwards. It also serves the purpose he stated in row 101 — *analytics is always scoped monthly* — which monthly close is exactly what makes final. December stops being a special case: its 15 Jan close is now just this rule. Three consequences on already-built work: (a) prior-period adjustment goes rare → routine, so the structured [prior period] field must carry the TARGET period and reports must show a month *as booked* vs *as belonging*; (b) T-106 §4's closed-period branch becomes the norm — the domain rule is right but the UI must DEFAULT reversalDate to today rather than erroring at the user; (c) subledger tie-out moves to a hard gate at every close, so a control-account break is caught in its own month. The soft "reviewed" marker is WITHDRAWN — closing the month is that signal, and stronger

title: Decision 105 (2026-08-24)
text: The opening balance is BALANCE-FORWARD per party — one lump AR/AP balance per party dated 2027-01-01, payments drawing it down oldest-first. No per-invoice open items are migrated (ADR-005 amendment) Why: Ian: *“the simplest cleanest approach as if we are just starting the business with a new book… allocation, leave it to me.”* Right, not merely convenient: an opening balance is a snapshot of POSITIONS, not a replay of history — Jan–Apr 2026 is already inside the 31 Dec figures, so nothing about it needs to reach the new system. Per-party lump sums are standard commercial practice when individual invoices are not imported, and invariant 6 survives intact (per-party balances must still sum exactly to the 2110, 1210 control). Balance-forward opening + open-item for new transactions coexist cleanly because the lump is dated first and is therefore always oldest. Pre-cutover aging and invoice detail live in Ian's spreadsheet, deliberately not in the system. 3900 must still net to exactly zero — the plug temptation is HIGHER with typed figures than with a load, and a residual halts rather than gets cleared. Consequence: T-115 (detail load) probably should not exist, and T-114b's audit becomes the deliverable — it tells Ian whether the numbers he is typing are right

title: Decision 107 (2026-08-24)
text: The income statement shows OPERATING INCOME and NET INCOME as two distinct lines. “Revenue − contra − COGS − opex” is operating income, NOT net income Why: My T-110 invariant 10 was wrong and the implementer was right to deviate. I wrote that formula and labelled it net income. The 7000-series — interest income, interest expense, other income — sits *below* operating profit and must still reach the bottom line, so the formula would have silently excluded every 7000 posting from net income. That is this project's founding defect reproduced for a different subset of accounts: v1's income statement is a hand-assembled scan list so a forgotten account is invisible; my formula would have made 7000 invisible by arithmetic instead of by omission — same outcome, harder to notice. Two lines is also the standard presentation, so the correction costs nothing and reads better. Adopted as the rule

title: Decision 110 (2026-08-24)
text: Inventory costing is FIFO Why: Ian, deciding ahead of the Phase 3 research pass. Defensible on physical grounds — food is perishable and actually moves first-in-first-out, so FIFO tracks reality rather than approximating it. Stated cost, once: FIFO needs cost layers (a remaining quantity and unit cost per receipt, consumed oldest-first) where weighted average needs one running number, so it is materially more implementation than the alternative. The Phase 3 research still runs — it now informs *how* to implement FIFO (layer storage, partial consumption, wastage against layers) rather than *whether*

title: Decision 114 (2026-08-25)
text: Access model: FOUR levels — super-admin (Ian, platform) › org admin (every org must have one) › store manager (a franchise's OWNER; one or more stores) › staff. manager means the SAME thing in Ian's org and in a franchise. Capabilities are STORE-SCOPED (T-121 §A) Why: Ian. A manager enrols staff, verifies and approves suppliers and buyers, and owns operational store settings — deliberately substantial, because it is the level at which the business actually runs. Buyer approval is a CREDIT decision, not merely operational, so *approving a buyer* and *setting how much they may owe* must be separable cells in the matrix. On super-admin I was too absolute: my draft said there is no global super-admin, but the platform operator is a real role — Ian restores backups and debugs failures. It must not be his everyday login, because he wears two hats: as platform operator he needs reach into every org, while as franchisor his contractual visibility is limited to SALES (ADR-008 §5). Break-glass instead — re-authentication, a stated reason, every use logged and visible. *“Did Ian look at my numbers?” must be answerable from a log, not from an assurance.* That protects Ian more than it constrains him. On who holds a franchise's org-admin: Ian holds it initially as an explicit grant of THAT org's admin role (never super-admin), transferable by data rather than by a release. And the concern that owners lack the technical know-how for admin points at the BUNDLE, not the owners — most of what

title: Decision 116 (2026-08-25)
text: Authority chain: only SUPER-ADMIN assigns an org's admin; that admin then sets managers' access; and when an admin is removed, managers' access changes ONLY if super-admin explicitly ticks it (CAPABILITY-MATRIX §B.2) Why: Ian. Completes row 115 rather than amending it, and closes a gap I left: §B said grants survive anyone's departure, but was silent on who re-elevates managers when an org genuinely has no admin left. Super-admin, by an explicit tick — the right role by elimination, since at that moment no admin exists. Assigning an admin stays with super-admin because who runs an org is a commercial decision, and because it stops an admin minting a peer admin, a lateral move invisible from above. Addition: the ABSENCE of a change must be visible. Not granting automatically is right; not noticing is not — an org could sit with no admin and un-elevated managers until someone cannot do their job, probably at month end. So deactivating an admin raises a notice to super-admin (*“Org X has no admin. Elevate its managers?”*) — a prompt, never an action. A design that refuses to escalate silently should also refuse to degrade silently. Known and accepted: two actions now depend on Ian personally

title: Decision 118 (2026-08-25)
text: STANDING PRINCIPLE — prefer the design that REMOVES a problem over the design that MANAGES it. Correctness is not negotiable; complexity beyond it is Why: Ian: *“for reference let's simplify future decisions like this… we could skip GRNI, it just adds a step and complexity. But don't get me wrong, I still want it to be correct — yet simplicity is better.”* This is feedback about HOW to decide, not only about GRNI. The test to apply: *does this machinery exist because the business has the problem, or because the pattern is standard?* GRNI solves “goods received, amount unknown” — a situation that does not arise here, because the price is agreed at order time and an agreed rate times an actual weight is still a known figure. Adopting it would have imported a solved problem from businesses that have it. Bible §1.1 already says the target is the midpoint; this row says how to find it when the correct-looking answer is also the more complex one

title: Decision 120 (2026-08-25)
text: Assigning the ADMIN role materialises a store-scope row for every store in that org. Rows, never a bypass. And creating a store must add rows for that org's existing admins (CAPABILITY-MATRIX §C.2) Why: The T-121 implementer took *“admin does not bypass store scope”* literally — correct — and that exposed a gap I left: an admin appointed today was authorised for nothing store-scoped, contradicting *“org admin = org-wide control”* (row 114). Both halves are right; the fix is row 115's own pattern — decide once, at the moment a human is present, and store the answer, rather than inferring it on every check. Keeps *“who can see Davao?”* a select. The easily-missed half: a store created LATER appears in nobody's scope, so store creation backfills admin rows — otherwise a new branch is invisible to the person who just opened it and it looks like a permissions bug rather than a missing row. Also recorded (§C.1): a capability answers “what may you do”, never “to whom”. manage_users cannot express row 116's authority chain alone — assigning the admin role additionally requires super_admin, and that check belongs at the call site with its own denial test

title: Decision 122 (2026-08-25)
text: A close-readiness checker runs daily 1st–15th. From the 16th, an unclosed prior month blocks back-office POSTING — never the till, never biometrics. Capture is always allowed; VERIFICATION is what is withheld (ADR-006 §8) Why: Ian. The checker is adopted as proposed and explains the window better than §7.2 did: the 15 days are the SETTLEMENT period, not slack — an August electricity bill arriving 10 September means August cannot close on 1 September. A recurring-expense template generates a CHECKLIST ITEM, never a posting: the amount varies so it cannot be automated, but the obligation is knowable, which beats auto-posting a figure nobody agreed. I pushed back on the wrong reading and Ian corrected it — I took “block transactions” to include the till; he meant back-office entry, with POS and biometrics running. The one real cost left was that blocking entry does not stop the expense, only its timely recording — trading this month's accuracy for last month's closure. His own sales-day answer generalised solves it: pending-and-unverifiable for all three. Record the draft with its photo while memory is fresh; withhold posting. A growing pile of unpostable drafts is a more legible signal than a greyed-out button, and it is visible to the admin who can act. Daily unlock kept, with a typed reason others can read — friction exercised daily becomes muscle memory by the third day

title: Decision 123 (2026-08-25)
text: close_period requires ORG-WIDE store scope for a manager — the last open matrix cell, now closed. And the OIL integrity-findings layer is PORTED from v1, with one gap fixed: a finding is DERIVED, only the ACKNOWLEDGEMENT is stored (T-135) Why: Ian. The scope answer keeps row 101 and row 114 both true: a period is org-wide, so a Lipa-only manager never closes Malvar's books. On OIL — I assumed “AI insights” meant AI-generated findings and was wrong; integrity.ts says *deterministic* and *pure observation layer, never touches the GL*, and both carry forward unchanged. Second time research has found v1 already at the correct shape. Two of its decisions are better than most systems manage: hardAlert fires through a snooze, closing the snooze-forever escape hatch, and thresholds default in code so a misconfig cannot disable detection. The gap: v1 stores state per finding key, so resolving one suppresses tomorrow's recompute while the condition still holds — the symptom hidden without the cause fixed. Fix: derive the finding, store only the acknowledgement. A finding cannot be resolved while it is still true; acknowledgement means *“seen and accepted for now”*, which is a different and honest statement. That also makes the manager scorecard safe — a score people are measured on is a score people manage, and this removes the way to game it. The close-readiness checker is a FILTER over this feed, not a second engine

title: Decision 124 (2026-08-25)
text: The 31 December cutover is a CONVERSION, not an onboarding wizard — and research corrected three of my own draft's decisions: ordering narrows to FOUR named gates, the REHEARSAL flag is dropped, and the opening entry is a mutable DRAFT until posting locks it (T-134, discovery 21) Why: I designed T-134 before researching it, which is backwards, and Ian said so: *“as always research before design.”* The pass found the draft's substance already right and its vocabulary wrong — “wizard/progress bar” pulled toward SaaS onboarding, where the real prior art is Xero's and Odoo's conversion: ~15 hardcoded steps, one correctness gate. Correction 1 — “not startable until prerequisites verify” was too strong. No reference system hard-blocks checklist steps on each other; hard gates live in close/reopen chains. Narrowed to A1→B1 (ADR-009's inversion), C2→C3, C3→C4, C4→C5 — everything else free-orderable. Correction 2 — no rehearsal flag. No system ships a rehearsal mode inside the live product; every one uses an isolated copy, which ADR-007 already provides, and ADR-007 §1 already rejected per-row markers for this exact reason: a flag is a marker a code path can forget to set. Correction 3 — C3 is a draft until C5 posts it. Xero and Odoo both treat the opening entry as editable until an explicit lock; forcing a formal reversal to fix a typo in a never-final document is ceremony, not control. Also added: an opening-count variance posts against 3900, NEVER 5400 — v2 has no December P&L, so

title: Decision 125 (2026-08-25)
text: A DRAFT expense is DELETED, and deleting it is governed by the EDIT capabilities — no new capability. And the 3900 halt stands, but the opening entry shows a RUNNING residual while you type (T-122 invariant 17, T-134) Why: Ian: *“delete for simplicity.”* Correct, and it closes a real hole — voidExpense refuses a draft (*“nothing has been posted yet to void”*) and nothing discarded one, so a mistaken draft had no ending at all. The justification is narrow and worth stating so it is never widened: a draft is not a financial record — no entry, no balance touched, nobody asserted it. Everything posted is still reversed, never removed. The capability choice is the interesting half: deleting a draft is the LAST EDIT you can make to it, so it reuses edit_own_expense / edit_any_expense rather than minting a delete_expense. There is no coherent answer under which a person may rewrite every field of a draft but not remove it (row 120), and reusing the pair means the 48-hour window cannot drift, because there is only one window. A cashier undoes their own mistake without finding a manager — friction on a self-correction is exactly what produces the abandoned drafts. On the halt: Ian asked whether to mirror the field, where Xero, Odoo and GnuCash all auto-plug an imbalance to suspense. Keep the halt — but the plug account buys those vendors TWO things and only one is bad. It makes the residual *visible* (good) and it makes the residual *postable* (bad). So C3 shows a running difference w

title: Decision 126 (2026-08-25)
text: An UNVERIFIED sales day records no revenue. A new sales report cannot be created while an older one is still unverified. And the entry dates on the SALES DAY, never the posting date (T-123) Why: Ian, answering the three-part question. Verification is what posts — a sales figure nobody checked is exactly what verification exists to catch, so an unverified day is a document, not an entry. The second half is his, and it is better than what I proposed. I suggested only dating on the business date, which fixes the period but lets an unverified day sit for weeks. Blocking a new report while an older one is unverified bounds the lag structurally — the pile cannot grow past one, so revenue is *hours* late rather than days, and the person who must act finds out immediately because they cannot do their next job until they do. A forcing function beats a reminder, and it is the same shape as row 122's unpostable-drafts pile: make the consequence immediate and visible to the person who can clear it. Dating on the sales day then puts a 31 December sale recorded on 2 January into December, where it happened — without which the block would merely relocate the error. Together the two rules make the close honest: the period cannot silently accumulate unrecognised revenue, and nothing lands in the wrong month

title: Decision 127 (2026-08-25)
text: Ian's cash-account OWNER split (cashier / office, each holding cash AND online) is retained — and v2 currently loses half of it: online has NO owner dimension at all Why: Ian: *“the accounts have 2 owners, cashier and office, and cashier has cash and online accounts… this will clearly show money movement.”* The model is right and answers the question a till reconciliation actually asks — whose hands is this money in. The gap, found checking rather than assuming: v2's chart keeps the split for cash (1110 cashier, 1120 staff custodian, 1130 office) but 1140 “E-wallet / online channels” is ONE control subdivided by PROVIDER, with no owner — so *“how much online money is in the cashier's hands versus the office's”* is unanswerable in v2 today. v1 does carry it, as owner?: 'cashier' \

title: Decision 129 (2026-08-25)
text: Remittance cadence is PER STORE, and an un-remitted CEILING forces a remittance regardless of where the cycle is. The mechanism is settled; the peso numbers are Ian's, per store (T-136 §4) Why: Ian: *“yes per store.”* Right — a branch two minutes from the office and one an hour away have genuinely different logistics, so a single global cadence would be wrong for at least one of them. Consequence: cadence is a configuration ROW, never a constant — and a store with none configured must not silently mean “never”. Default to daily, the safe end, and what every store does today; an unset cadence is the same defect class as an unmapped expense category. Per-store cadence makes the ceiling MORE necessary, not less — a store on a weekly cadence accumulates seven days of cash, and ₱200/day versus ₱20,000/day is the same number of days and a completely different amount sitting in a drawer. The risk is the AMOUNT, not the days, so the pooled balance is watched continuously and crossing the ceiling forces a remittance mid-cycle — the same shape as row 122's checker, which watches the condition rather than only the deadline. “Forces” means what it means everywhere else here: the pile becomes visible and unignorable to the person who can clear it, never a blocked till. A cashier is never stopped from selling because a remittance is overdue (discovery 22 §4). I settled the mechanism and deliberately did NOT pick the numbers — a peso ceiling and an imprest amount are business policy, and th

title: Decision 131 (2026-08-25)
text: The cash-custody research: the account is UNDEPOSITED FUNDS (I had the term wrong), the till reconciles PER CASHIER PER SHIFT with denomination counts, v1's less/plus is AHEAD of ERPNext — and a mandatory per-transaction PWD/senior LOGBOOK exists that nothing captures today (discovery 24) Why: Correction first: I wrote “cash in transit / undeposited funds” in rows 127 and 128 as if interchangeable and they are not. *Undeposited funds* is our books versus where the money physically is; *deposit in transit* is our books versus the bank's — a bank-reconciliation timing item with nothing to do with a till. Using the wrong one would have invited someone to reconcile a till against a bank statement. Row 129's ceiling is retro-justified by the field: vendors describe batched deposits as the ordinary case for undeposited funds, AND warn it is *“one of the accounts most likely to cause a business's financial statements to be incorrect”* because money piles up in it forever when the deposit step is never done. A pooled-remittance design without a ceiling is that failure with extra steps. From ERPNext's POS Opening/Closing Entry, three things to adopt: reconciliation per cashier per shift (v1 is per store per day, which cannot attribute a variance when two cashiers worked — and attribution is the whole custody control), denomination-level counting (quantity of each note and coin, not one total), and expected/closing/difference PER PAYMENT METHOD, which is row 127's owner/instrument spli

title: Decision 132 (2026-08-25)
text: Senior/PWD discounts stay CONTRA-REVENUE (4900). The till reconciles PER SHIFT and the sales day stays PER DAY — both, not one. And the statutory discount LOGBOOK becomes a requirement: ~~today only the ID is captured~~ — THAT HALF IS FALSE, corrected by row 164 Why: Ian, answering discovery 24's three opens. One reading stated rather than assumed: he answered *“contra asset”*, and I am taking that as contra-REVENUE — the choice on the table was contra-revenue (4900, current) versus BIR's *“Expenses – PWD Discounts”*, and *contra* is the operative half. A sales discount is not a contra-asset (that class is accumulated depreciation, allowance for doubtful accounts — a valuation account against something the business owns). So 4900 stands unchanged and POSTING-PATTERNS.md's sale.discount.senior-pwd needs no edit. If he meant something else this is the line to correct. Per shift AND per day is the right answer and it settles T-123 §3's decomposition: the till position (split B) is per cashier per shift, which is what makes a variance attributable to one person; the sales day (split A) stays per store per day, which is what revenue recognition and the period close need. Shifts roll up into a day — they are not competing grains, they are two levels of one hierarchy, and v1 already carries both (its derive-totals.ts branches on whether it is writing a shift doc or a day doc). ~~On the logbook: today the business captures only the ID.~~ CORRECTED BY ROW 164 — nothing captures an ID

text: ONLY AN ADMIN MAY ADD AN ACCOUNT TO THE BOOKS — a standing rule, not a decision about one screen. The gate is manage_chart_of_accounts (org-scoped, admin and super-admin only). Why: Ian: *“only admin can add accounts to the books”* … *“that must be the rule.”* Recorded because I got it wrong first, and the wrong reasoning is the instructive part. text: MOVING money between accounts is MANAGER level; OPENING one stays admin-only. New capability transfer_funds (store-scoped, manager and up). Why: Ian: *“yes manager level money transfer.”* The pairing with row 149 is the decision, not the level. A transfer changes nothing about the books' shape — it RECORDS something that already happened to money that is already there. Those are different acts and they earn different levels. The concrete test: a manager may already accept_remittance, which is the single largest transfer this business makes (a whole day's takings, cashier to office). Barring that same manager from moving ₱500 between two drawers would be incoherent. transfer_funds is manager-TRUE, so it does NOT join — that set is derived as admin-yes/manager-no, and a manager holds this one outright. Nothing to grant, nothing to remember. title: Decision 154 (2026-08-26)
text: OVERDRAFT IS A PROPERTY OF THE ACCOUNT, NOT OF THE FEATURE. A CASHIER account is WARNED and still posts; an OFFICE or STAFF account is REFUSED. Supersedes row 153's blanket block. Refusing there refuses a shortfall that is not real, and nothing drives people to work around a system faster than being told they have no money while they are looking at it. No other custodian has that gap: an office safe or a staff float only ever receives money through a transfer, cash request or liquidation, all of which post the moment they happen — so its balance is COMPLETE, a negative is a real error, and it stays refused. The rule therefore turns on custodian, never on which screen the money left through, which is why it lives in ONE file (money-accounts/overdraft.ts) that both approveExpense and createMoneyTransfer call. title: Decision 157 (2026-08-27)
text: WHAT IS REMITTED IS THE END-DAY REPORT, NOT THE SALES REPORT — and they are ONE thing, not two. A day is owed the CASHIER'S NET MOVEMENT for that date, not its remittable sales. text: A CASHIER DRAWER'S OVERDRAFT IS CAPPED, PER ACCOUNT, AND ADMIN SETS IT. ROW 154's WARNING NOW HAS A FLOOR. Why: Ian: *“how deep can a cashier account be negative — it can't be unlimited, so admin can set it. If the set is 20,000 that is the only allowable negative balance a cashier is allowed to.”* Row 154's reasoning was right and had no floor of its own. A till's true balance is unknowable until the day is verified — the cash is in the drawer before it is in the ledger — so a shortfall is a *“look at this”*, not a *“you are wrong”*. But that argument justifies a drawer being ₱2,000 behind and equally ₱2,000,000 behind. The first is a bookkeeping lag; the second is a missing drawer, and nothing in the ledger could tell them apart. Zero is meaningful: it means that drawer may never go below zero at all, which is why a blank field on the form means *“leave it alone”* and not *“set it to zero”*. title: Decision 282 (2026-10-05)

text: OPENING STOCK IS COUNTED PER ROOM AT THE COMMISSARY AND IN ONE ROOM AT EACH BRANCH, AND IS VALUED AT THE LAST V1 DELIVERY PRICE; AN ITEM V1 NEVER DELIVERED IS PRICED BY A MANAGER TYPING IT. title: Decision 319 (2026-10-14)
text: THE TILL STAYS IN THE ERP; THE POS v2 SCREEN MIRRORS IT. Ian (Q1 of docs/feedback/2026-10-14-ian-feedback-review.md): *"a"*. Till custody (open shift, count, close, charge a shortage, remittance; T-186, T-153, T-143, T-366) stays an ERP record. Why: A POS-owned handover cannot see cashier-paid expenses, cash requests or AP paid from the drawer, so it would force a second entry (review item 1)

title: Decision 320 (2026-10-14)
text: SETTLEMENT FILES ARE PARSED, NOT RETYPED: A GRAB OR FOODPANDA PAYOUT FILE IN ZIP, XLS/XLSX OR PDF BECOMES A DRAFT SETTLEMENT THAT A PERSON POSTS THROUGH THE EXISTING ACTION. NOTHING IS WRITTEN TO v1. Ian (Q2): *"a - it must accept zip xls and pdf files that it will parse and post"*. The parser only fills the input of recordChannelSettlement (same capability, same idempotency, same patterns channel_settlement.plain / .promo_credit); it has no posting path of its own. The store is chosen explicitly on upload, never routed from the filename (v1's "lip 15.zip" → Lipa, discovery 23; row 283). A file or line that does not parse is quarantined with its reason and never half-posted (§5 rule 5); the uploaded file is kept as the settlement's evidence. "Mirrored to v1" means the read-only dual-run comparison (T-392 S1b), so rows 78 and 106 stand. Narrows T-150 ("manual entry first; the parsers are their own task"): that task is now ordered, and manual entry stays as the fallback. Platform *sales* are untouched (row 130): this is the payout, not the sale. Why: Ian's ruling

title: Decision 324 (2026-10-14)
text: SOME EXPENSE CATEGORIES NEED NO RECEIPT AT ALL: A TRUE, PER-CATEGORY EXEMPTION. Ian (Q6): *"a"*. A category carries a flag "no receipt needed", and an expense in it posts with no evidence. Reverses T-196 decision 2 ("evidence stays unconditional; needReceipts is not ported"). How exempt spend stays visible and controlled, binding on the spec: (1) only an admin sets the flag, under its own capability, and every change is an audit_log event (T-402 tag), never a silent edit; (2) the flag is stamped onto each expense when it is created, so turning it on later never exempts old spend and turning it off never strands it; (3) a "spend without a receipt" register per store × month (amount, category, who, approver) sits on the manager and admin dashboards; this is the orphan detector T-196's out-of-scope note said an exemption needs; (4) approval, overdraft (rows 154, 321) and the manual doubtful flag (T-363, row 251) apply unchanged; (5) the category list marks the exempt ones plainly. v1 exempted only "Employee Expenses / Incentive", so the seeded default is that one category and every other exemption is an admin act. Whether an exempt expense still needs its supplier-invoice record (T-196) or none at all is a spec question. Why: Ian's ruling. v1's orphan expenses came from the flag with no detector, so the detector ships with the flag

title: Decision 326 (2026-10-14)
text: CONVERT STAYS THE UNPAID SAME-SLAB RE-CUT; SLICING GAINS PAID/UNPAID, WHO SLICED, AND THE PIECE RATE. Ian (Q8): *"a"*. T-176 §4 stands ("the re-cut constraint is the whole point; do not relax it"). A slice record carries performed_by_person_id, paid/unpaid and a piece rate; a paid slice is what slicer pay reads (hasLiveSlicerPaymentCovering, a stub today). This pulls the recording half of slicer pay forward from Phase 5 (CAPABILITY-GAPS); paying it stays in payroll. Why: Ian's ruling

title: Decision 328 (2026-10-14)
text: A CUSTOMER PRICE LIST STORES THE RULE; EACH ORDER LINE FREEZES THE RATE. Ian (Q10): *"a"*. The list keeps a rate mode (fixed, ±% or ±₱ over a named basis: item cost or the branch price, mirroring item_pricing.pricing_mode). The unit is always the item's base unit (the free-text price_list_items.unit goes). An order line copies the computed rate when it is made, so a later rule change never re-prices history (discovery 19 §3.4). Why: Ian's ruling

title: Decision 331 (2026-10-14)
text: THE ERP CUSTOMER SCREEN ALSO SHOWS A DINER'S LOYALTY PROFILE. Ian (Q13): *"yes"*. This needs a new link between an AR customer and a diner person (ADR-008 §11 keeps them apart; row 273: a diner is a person with a phone identity). The link is optional, made by a person, and audited; points stay a liability of the issuing org (row 273). Built at ADR-015 P3 with loyalty. text: DUAL RUN: THE V2 ENCODER ALSO ENTERS GRAB/FOODPANDA PAYOUTS. The POS pull compares expected (sold x rule) against posted actual and flags a gap beyond ±10%; once T-401 S6 lands it no longer takes stock out. (4) A payroll run whose month was already paid to an agency cannot be voided until that agency payment is voided first; the books never show an agency as overpaid by accident (q-t193-void-paid-month a).
