title: Expense payment (expense_payment) — 4,396 legs, 34% of activity, #1
text: v1 posts the funding leg(s) only (cash / AP / online OUT) and never the classification leg — bible §16.0's diagnosis in one word. Every pattern below restores the missing expense line.

title: expense.cash.simple — Cash expense, single payment
text:
A ₱1,200 delivery of pork paid in cash from the cashier drawer. A COGS category (meat) is expensed directly on receipt — the correct Phase 1 treatment. The two-stage purchase→inventory→consumption posting (COA-ALIGNMENT §4.1) needs real inventory tracking, which is Phase 3; until then a COGS purchase is the same shape as any other cash expense, just posted to a 5xxx account instead of a 6xxx one.
5100 COGS — food - 1,200.00 - —
1110 Cash on hand — cashier - 1,200.00 - —
Trap: do not "wait for Phase 3" before posting expenses — the classification leg is required now; the two-stage inventory refinement changes *where* the debit lands later, it is not a reason to omit it today.

title: expense.split.cash-online — Split-payment expense, one entry, several credit lines
text:
A ₱3,500 supplies order paid ₱2,000 from the cashier drawer and ₱1,500 from an online wallet. The single most common shape in the whole v1 dataset: one expense, several payment methods, one journal entry with several credit lines.
6500 Supplies - 3,500.00 - —
1110 Cash on hand — cashier - 2,000.00 - —
1140 E-wallet / online channels - 1,500.00 - money_account:gcash-cashier

title: expense.credit.ap — Credit expense, books to AP
text:
A ₱8,000 supplies order on 30-day terms from a named supplier. No cash moves; the obligation grows the AP control account instead.
6500 Supplies - 8,000.00 - —
2110 Accounts payable - 8,000.00 - supplier
Trap: 2110 is a control account (T-118, ) — every credit-method payment must carry the supplier as a party or the database rejects the line outright. A credit expense with no supplierId quarantines rather than posting an unattributable control line.

title: expense.reimbursable — Reimbursable expense, staff paid out of pocket
text:
A staff member fronted ₱650 for an emergency repair. The company now owes them — a liability, not an asset (COA-ALIGNMENT §3 answer #1: *"we owe to staff — staff own money they spend for business needs"*).
6600 Repairs and maintenance - 650.00 - —
2130 Reimbursements payable to employees - 650.00 - employee
Trap: reimbursement is expense-first, cash-later — the opposite of a salary advance (cash-first, an asset). Booking this as an asset is the live v1 misclassification COA-ALIGNMENT corrects: today it defaults to the debit side because inferAccountNature has no rule for staff_reimbursable, understating liabilities.

title: reimbursement.payout — Settling the reimbursement above
text:
The ₱650 owed from expense.reimbursable is paid out in cash. Pure balance sheet — the expense was already recognised when the liability was created.
2130 Reimbursements payable to employees - 650.00 - employee
1110 Cash on hand — cashier - 650.00 - —

title: reimbursement.payout-cross-store — Paid from another store's safe
text:
The same ₱650, owed at Lipa, paid out of Malvar's office safe. One entry: the safe's credit sits at the safe's store, the debt stays at Lipa, and the pair between the stores records who now owes whom.
2130 Reimbursements payable to employees - Lipa - 650.00 - employee
2150 Due to related store - Lipa - 650.00 - store (Malvar)
1250 Due from related store - Malvar - 650.00 - store (Lipa)
1130 Cash on hand — office - Malvar - 650.00 - —
Trap: the credit at the owing store balances perfectly and is wrong: balanceOf reads the safe at the safe's store, so the paying safe never moves and the owing store's cash goes negative (). An expense_payment or ap_payment drawn on another store's account has exactly the same shape.
---

title: sale.unli.simple — Dine-in unlimited, cash only
text:
A ₱5,600 day of pure unli sales, paid entirely in cash. dineInSales maps straight to 4100 — GLOSSARY.md: dineInSales means unlimited-package sales only, not "all dine-in", and it needs no reconstruction because POS already computes it that way.
1110 Cash on hand — cashier - 5,600.00 - —
4100 Food sales — unlimited (unli) - 5,600.00 - —

title: sale.alacarte.simple — À la carte, includes take-out and delivery
text:
A ₱780 day of à la carte sales, cash only. takeOutSales is the field name, but GLOSSARY.md warns it is a residual — Math.max(0, totalGross - dineInSales) — that absorbs dine-in à la carte, take-out, and delivery alike, because POS has no take-out flag at all (COA-ALIGNMENT §2: 4200 was withdrawn for exactly this reason). It all posts to 4150.
1110 Cash on hand — cashier - 780.00 - —
4150 Food sales — à la carte (dine-in, take-out and delivery) - 780.00 - —
Trap: takeOutSales is not a measurement of take-out orders — never chart it as one. A non-zero value is everything that is not unli, all mixed together. Treat it as a reconciliation signal, never a revenue breakdown.

title: sale.discount.senior-pwd — Senior/PWD discount, contra-revenue
text:
A ₱1,000 unli sale with a ₱200 senior-citizen discount; ₱800 cash actually tendered. In v1 this discount is hardcoded to zero on the live sales-entry path (bible §16.7 defect #3) — this worked example is what it should be, and the gap is the finding.
1110 Cash on hand — cashier - 800.00 - —
4900 Sales discounts - 200.00 - —
4100 Food sales — unlimited (unli) - 1,000.00 - —
Trap: no VAT is computed anywhere. This discount reduces revenue for internal management reporting; it is not a BIR VAT-exemption computation and must never be presented as one.

title: sale.comps — Comps, contra-revenue, never marketing expense
text:
A ₱500 unli sale where ₱100 was comped (given away complimentary); ₱400 cash tendered. Ian confirmed directly: comps are revenue foregone, never a cost incurred.
1110 Cash on hand — cashier - 400.00 - —
4950 Sales returns and voids - 100.00 - —
4100 Food sales — unlimited (unli) - 500.00 - —
Trap: comps post to 4950 (Sales returns and voids), not 4900 (Sales discounts) — confirmed by bible decision-log row 74 (*"comps are contra-revenue (4950), not marketing expense"*), docs/GLOSSARY.md's own comps entry, and packages/etl/src/convert.ts's already-tested ACCOUNTS.SALES_RETURNS_AND_VOIDS mapping. T-108's own original task spec text said "DR 4900" for comps — that line was wrong, contradicted by three independent, already-decided sources, and is reported as a spec defect in the T-108 task report rather than followed. 4900 is reserved for senior/PWD/other discounts; comps are a distinct account.

title: sale.mixed — The full pattern: cash, online, unli, à la carte, discount and comps together
text:
A ₱5,450 day: ₱3,000 cash, ₱2,000 online, ₱300 discount, ₱150 comps, ₱4,450 of it unli and ₱1,000 à la carte. The complete shape every module should copy — debits (tender + contra-revenue) first, credits (revenue) last.
1110 Cash on hand — cashier - 3,000.00 - —
1140 E-wallet / online channels - 2,000.00 - money_account:gcash-main
4900 Sales discounts - 300.00 - —
4950 Sales returns and voids - 150.00 - —
4100 Food sales — unlimited (unli) - 4,450.00 - —
4150 Food sales — à la carte - 1,000.00 - —
Trap: the balance identity is two separate checks, not one — (1) cash + online + discounts + comps = totalSales (the tender side), and (2) dineInSales + takeOutSales = totalSales (the revenue side). A sales day that fails either quarantines rather than posting a guessed entry.

title: sale.pos-correction — POS changed a verified day afterwards (T-375 S6)
text:
v2-only. POS can void a receipt or edit a closed one after the day was verified and posted. The day's own entry and figures never change (a linked day's figures are locked to the POS derivation, and history is a new fact, not an edit); a manager posts a correcting entry: the checked feed's journal lines minus what the ledger already holds for the day. Example (D1 day posted at ₱1,050 paid; POS later shows a voided ₱50 cash receipt, ₱1,000 paid):
4100 Food sales — unlimited (unli) - 50.00 - —
1110 Cash on hand — cashier - 50.00 - —

title: sale.platform-correction — the platform file is higher than staff typed (T-511 S6b)
text:
v2-only. Staff typed a ₱9,000 Foodpanda day and it was verified and posted (Dr 1220 ₱9,000 / Cr 4150 ₱9,000). The platform statement for that day says ₱10,000. The staff figure and the day's own entry stay as they are; the file figure is the truth for sales and the receivable, so approving the file posts the difference as a correcting entry (correctPlatformSales):
1220 Channel receivable - 1,000.00 - channel
4150 Food sales — à la carte - 1,000.00 - —
Rule. delta = file figure − old, where old is what the ledger holds for that channel and day: the channel's 1220 on the day's entry plus its earlier platform corrections, read from journal_lines — never sales_day_channels.amount, which is never overwritten. A positive delta is the pair above; a negative one is the same pair the other way round (next pattern); zero posts nothing at all.

title: sale.platform-correction-lower — the platform file is lower than staff typed (T-511 S6b, )
text:
Staff typed an ₱11,000 Foodpanda day; the statement says ₱10,000. Without a correction the settlement clears ₱10,000 and ₱1,000 stays stuck on 1220 with no sweep (). The correcting entry is the same two accounts on the opposite sides:
4150 Food sales — à la carte - 1,000.00 - —
1220 Channel receivable - 1,000.00 - channel
The settlement of ₱10,000 then clears the receivable to exactly zero.
Trap: a negative delta is the same two accounts on the opposite sides, not a different pair and not a negative amount. The revenue account is the one the original sales-day posting used (4150), never a new one.

title: sale.pos-short-payment — the POS took a few centavos less than the bill (T-558, bible row 459)
text:
v2-only, POS-derived days. A cashier may accept a payment up to pos.sale_variance_tolerance (default ₱0.01, cap ₱0.10) below the bill; anything larger is still accepted but flagged as a high-severity shortfall (T-558). The day's receipts total ₱1,000.00 of unli; the tenders total ₱999.99 cash, because one receipt was paid one centavo short. Revenue stays at the full receipt prices; the tender line shows what was actually taken; the gap is booked to 7350.
1110 Cash on hand — cashier - 999.99 - —
7350 Cash over and short - 0.01 - —
4100 Food sales — unlimited (unli) - 1,000.00 - —
Rule. The variance is not a stored figure: at routing time it is gross − Σ tenders − Σ discounts − Σ comps for the day's receipts, and it posts as one 7350 debit line when it is above zero. Both balance checks of sale.mixed then hold with the variance counted on the tender side: tenders + discounts + comps + variance = totalSales.

title: sale.pos-refund-excess — a POS method refunded more than it took in the Z (T-614 S1, )
text:
v2-only, POS Z (writeZ, postRefundExcessForZ). A refund of an earlier day's sale comes out of the till on the day it is given. If a method's refunds in the Z's window are more than that method's takings, the method nets below zero, and the sales day cannot hold a negative cash or wallet figure. Example: cash refunded ₱750.00 against ₱250.00 of cash taken. The sales day floors cash at 0 and its refunds figure drops by the same excess (₱750.00 − ₱500.00 = ₱250.00 left on the day). The excess ₱500.00 posts as its own entry at the Z, dated the Z business date. A wallet does the same on 1140 with its money account as the party.
4950 Sales returns and voids - 500.00 - —
1110 Cash on hand — cashier - 500.00 - —
Rule. One entry per method over its takings: source_type 'pos_refund_excess', idempotency key pos_refund_excess:<closeId>:<cash|moneyAccountId>, so a replayed Z writes nothing twice. Live stores only: test mode books nothing. The day's own entry (sale.mixed) plus this one leave the money place lower by the full refund and 4950 up by it.

title: sale.pos-deposit-applied — a bill paid partly from a held reservation deposit (T-628)
text:
v2-only, POS Z (deriveSalesDayFromZ, routeSalesDay). A customer who booked a table left a deposit; at the bill the cashier applies it as a payment line "Deposit". Example: a ₱1,000.00 à la carte bill, ₱500.00 from the deposit and ₱500.00 in cash. The deposit was booked on the day it was taken (deposit.taken), so on the sales day it is a tender of the sale: the day's deposits_applied figure is on the collected side of the reconciliation and posts as a debit to 2170.
1110 Cash on hand — cashier - 500.00 - —
2170 Customer deposits payable - 500.00 - —
4150 Food sales — à la carte - 1,000.00 - —
Rule. Applying is consume-once: one applied event per reservation and per receipt (partial unique indexes), written in the sale's own transaction; a second apply is refused and, arriving later from an offline tablet, the sale is quarantined. The deposit never exceeds the bill or what is held. It is a POS-derived day figure only (a typed or feed day has none, CHECK).
Trap: never count the deposit as cash collected on the day of the bill: it was already counted on the day it was taken, and counting it again makes the drawer look richer than it is.

title: deposit.taken — a table reservation deposit is taken (T-628)
text:
v2-only, POS Z (postDepositsForZ). A customer pays ₱1,000.00 in cash to hold a table. The money is in the till that day, so the Z of the till that took it posts it beside the sales day, store-scoped:
1110 Cash on hand — cashier - 1,000.00 - —
2170 Customer deposits payable - 1,000.00 - —
Rule. One entry per kind per money place per Z (a wallet is 1140 with its money account as party), source_type 'pos_deposit', idempotency key pos_deposit:<closeId>:<kind>:<place>. The event can be taken offline (inbox deposit.taken) and counts in the drawer of the day it was taken. Live stores only: test mode books nothing.
Trap: never book a deposit as sales or other income when it is taken: nothing is earned until the table is billed (it is applied) or a manager keeps it.

title: Salary advance (salary_advance) — 1,488 legs, #3
text: Disbursement and repayment (the common cases) are pure balance sheet, never P&L — only the rarer "charge" txType touches a counter account. 1230 is a requires_party control account (party = employee).

title: salary_advance.disbursement — Cash out, an asset grows
text:
A staff member draws a ₱3,000 salary advance in cash. An advance is cash-first — an asset — the mirror image of a reimbursement (expense-first, a liability).
1230 Advances to employees - 3,000.00 - employee
1110 Cash on hand — cashier - 3,000.00 - —

title: salary_advance.repayment — A payroll deduction settles it
text:
A ₱500 payroll deduction repays part of the same advance.
1110 Cash on hand — cashier - 500.00 - —
1230 Advances to employees - 500.00 - employee
Trap: most salary_advance legs (disbursement, repayment) never touch P&L — only the rare "charge" txType does, and even then the counter-account is caller-supplied. Do not assume this sourceType is nominal by default.
---

title: Transfer (transfer) — 926 legs, #4
text: "Source OUT + target IN, both balance-sheet" — but a genuine finding: with a fee, a third leg posts to an expense account. Not party-requiring — ordinary asset-to-asset cash movement, not inter-store in the ordinary case — a cross-store transfer between two offices has carried the due-from/due-to pair since T-139, and transfer.settle-between-stores below is the one that repays it. (A dispatch of goods is commissary_dispatch, below.)

title: transfer.cash.simple — Cashier drawer to the office
text:
A routine ₱15,000 move from the cashier drawer to the office safe.
1130 Cash on hand — office - 15,000.00 - —
1110 Cash on hand — cashier - 15,000.00 - —

title: transfer.cash.with-fee — With a bank fee, NOT always pure balance sheet
text:
A ₱10,000 online-to-office transfer costs a ₱50 bank fee, so only ₱9,950 lands.
1130 Cash on hand — office - 9,950.00 - —
6870 Bank charges - 50.00 - —
1140 E-wallet / online channels - 10,000.00 - money_account:gcash-main
Trap: do not assume every transfer is P&L-free. When a fee applies, a real expense leg exists and must be included — omitting it would silently understate the fee expense while the entry still balances (the entry balances either way; only the *account* would be wrong).

title: transfer.settle-between-stores — Paying back what one store owes another
text:
Lipa repays the ₱650 it owes Malvar, from Lipa's office safe to Malvar's. The cash legs are a normal transfer; the clearing pair then takes the debt off both stores' books in the same single entry.
1130 Cash on hand — office - Malvar - 650.00 - —
1250 Due from related store - Malvar - 650.00 - store (Lipa)
2150 Due to related store - Lipa - 650.00 - store (Malvar)
1130 Cash on hand — office - Lipa - 650.00 - —
Trap: an ordinary transfer back posts DR 1250 at the payer, which grosses both debts up instead of clearing them (). Only a settlement debits 2150 at the payer and credits 1250 at the payee, and it is capped by what both stores' books say is owed.
---

title: Depreciation (depreciation) — 362 legs, #5
text: Always both legs, no conditionality. One of ADR-005's five capabilities that "cannot wait past January."

title: Loan payment and disbursement (loan_payment 221 legs / loan_disbursement 4 legs)
text: Disbursement is always pure balance sheet (no interest leg, ever); payment is nominal only when interestAmount > 0. 2400 requires party — the loan itself, filed under party_type = 'loan', party = the loan (see the trap below).

title: loan_payment.principal-only — Zero P&L lines
text:
A ₱5,000 principal-only repayment on a term loan.
2400 Loans payable - 5,000.00 - loan
1110 Cash on hand — cashier - 5,000.00 - —
Trap: 2400's party_type is "loan" and the party is the loan, not the lender and not a supplier (LOAN_PARTY_TYPE in repo/loans.ts). Do not file it under "supplier".

title: loan_payment.with-interest — The conditional P&L leg appears
text:
A ₱4,800 instalment: ₱4,500 principal, ₱300 interest.
2400 Loans payable - 4,500.00 - supplier
7200 Interest expense - 300.00 - —
1110 Cash on hand — cashier - 4,800.00 - —

title: loan_disbursement.simple — Cash in, a liability grows, never P&L
text:
A ₱50,000 term loan is drawn down.
1110 Cash on hand — cashier - 50,000.00 - —
2400 Loans payable - 50,000.00 - supplier
---

title: AR collection with a platform fee (ar_collection) — 176 legs
text: The marquee example. v1 recognised a platform fee twice and it cost ₱198,148.29 across two stores, 37 duplicate expense documents voided (discovery 06 §3.2). Three legs, always distinct: gross receivable cleared, cash actually received, fee expensed — never any other combination.

title: ar_collection.with-platform-fee — The double-count this prevents
text:
A ₱5,000 receivable from a Grab settlement collects with a ₱250 platform fee deducted at source; only ₱4,750 actually lands in the bank.
1110 Cash on hand — cashier - 4,750.00 - — - grab
6400 Platform and channel fees - 250.00 - — - grab
1210 Accounts receivable - 5,000.00 - customer - grab
Trap: this platform fee is booked here, once, as part of the collection. It must never also be booked as a separate expense document for the same settlement — that double posting is the confirmed v1 defect that cost ₱198,148.29. A module that both posts this collection AND lets someone manually expense "platform fee" for the same settlement has reintroduced the bug.

title: ar_collection.no-fee — The conditional leg genuinely absent
text:
A ₱2,000 receivable collects in full, no platform fee applies. Two legs only — 6400 does not appear at all.
1110 Cash on hand — cashier - 2,000.00 - —
1210 Accounts receivable - 2,000.00 - customer

title: ar_collection.cross-store — Paid into another store's safe
text:
The same ₱2,000 receivable, owed at Lipa, is paid into Malvar's office safe. One entry: the cash debit sits at the safe's store, the receivable stays at Lipa, and the pair between the stores records who now owes whom.
1130 Cash on hand — office - Malvar - 2,000.00 - —
2150 Due to related store - Malvar - 2,000.00 - store (Lipa)
1250 Due from related store - Lipa - 2,000.00 - store (Malvar)
1210 Accounts receivable - Lipa - 2,000.00 - customer
Trap: money landing at another store makes THAT store the debtor — the pair runs opposite to reimbursement.payout-cross-store. The debit at the owing store balances perfectly and is wrong: balanceOf reads the safe at the safe's store, so the receiving safe never rises (). A loan_payment drawn on another store's safe has the payout direction; a loan_disbursement drawn into one has this direction.
---

title: AP payment (ap_payment) — 93 legs
text: "Source cash/online OUT + ap OUT (allocated) + optional supplier_advance IN (overpayment)." Bible §16.10's own rule: overpayment goes to a named home account, never to nowhere.

title: ap_payment.simple — Clears exactly what is owed
text:
A ₱12,000 payment to a supplier, applied exactly against the outstanding AP balance.
2110 Accounts payable - 12,000.00 - supplier
1110 Cash on hand — cashier - 12,000.00 - —

title: ap_payment.from_float — AP payment from a cash-request float, the 1120 leg names the request
text:
A ₱600 supplier payment drawn from a released ₱1,000 cash-request float, through the store's staff cash account. The 1120 credit carries the request as its party, so the float falls to ₱400 and the ledger still says whose money it was. Only the cash portion draws the float; the request is locked and its live balance checked first (T-415). See the 1120-party rule below.
2110 Accounts payable - 600.00 - supplier
1120 Staff cash - 600.00 - cash_request

title: ap_payment.overpayment — Never floats to nowhere
text:
An ₱8,000 AP balance is paid with ₱8,500, ₱500 more than owed.
2110 Accounts payable - 8,000.00 - supplier
1240 Advances to suppliers - 500.00 - supplier
1110 Cash on hand — cashier - 8,500.00 - —
Trap: payments must name the open items they settle. Overpayment goes to 1240 (Advances to suppliers) — a real, party-carrying asset — never to an unallocated cash-in-limbo state. The same supplier both owes and is owed simultaneously here, and that is correct, not a contradiction.
---

title: Supplier return (supplier_return) — v2-only, bible row 166
text: "The goods go back, and we hold a credit." Which credit leg fires is DERIVED at post time from whether the receipt being returned against carries a linked supplier invoice — never a user choice (T-170 invariant 5).

title: supplier.return-grni — no credit arises, nothing is owed yet
text:
Returning 10 kg of a 30 kg receipt that has NOT been invoiced. The supplier will simply bill for less; there is nothing to credit.
2120 Goods received not invoiced - 1,000.00 - —
1310 Inventory — raw materials - 1,000.00 - —

title: supplier.return-credit — a real, spendable credit
text:
Returning 10 kg of a receipt that HAS been invoiced. 1240 already exists as a party-carrying asset (the same account an AP overpayment lands in, ap_payment.overpayment above) — a return credit and an overpayment are the same fact: money the supplier owes back.
1240 Advances to suppliers - 1,000.00 - supplier
1310 Inventory — raw materials - 1,000.00 - —
Trap: never a supplier_credits table and never a credit_balance column — the balance is a query over 1240's own party-filtered lines ('s pattern, refused the ninth time). Not a negative balance netted into 2110 either: that would put a debit in a liability control account and hide the credit inside "what we owe."

title: supplier.credit-applied — spending it against a later invoice
text:
The credit drawn down inside ap_payment's own posting (T-130 §5's extension), not a separate document type. A ₱1,000 invoice paid ENTIRELY from an existing ₱1,000 credit — no cash moves.
2110 Accounts payable - 1,000.00 - supplier
1240 Advances to suppliers - 1,000.00 - supplier
Trap: the money-account leg of ap_payment is a zero-amount line here and is OMITTED — moneyAccountId is still named on the payment record (ADR-010: always a real account, never a label), even though no draw happens against it that day. A refund (cash paid back instead of applied) posts the mirror image — Dr the money account, Cr 1240 — and is also not a new document type.
---

title: Customer return (customer_return) — T-179, bible row 166
text: T-170's shape pointing the other way — but not symmetric, and the asymmetry is named rather than hidden: a supplier return reverses two things (cost, stock); a customer return reverses three (revenue, cost, stock), because we recognised revenue on the way out and did not on the way in.

title: customer.return-ar — still owed — reduces the receivable directly
text:
A ₱5,000 wholesale line, costing ₱900, returned in full. The customer had not paid yet.
4950 Sales returns and voids - 5,000.00
1210 Accounts receivable - 5,000.00 - customer
1310 Inventory - 900.00
5100 COGS - 900.00
Trap: never a debit to 4300 directly (invariant 3) — netting a return into revenue hides the return rate, a number a wholesale operation manages. The cost leg is what the SALE's own consumption actually relieved, read from stock_layer_consumptions — never recomputed from today's layers (§5 of the task spec).

title: customer.return-credit — already paid — a real, spendable credit
text:
A ₱500 line, costing ₱90, returned by a customer who has already paid in full. 2140 is party-required, the same account an AR overpayment already lands in.
4950 Sales returns and voids - 500.00
2140 Customer store credits payable - 500.00 - customer
1310 Inventory - 90.00
5100 COGS - 90.00
Trap: never a customer_credits table and never a credit_balance column — the balance is a query over 2140's own party-filtered lines ('s pattern). A return exceeding what is still owed splits across both 1210 and 2140 in this SAME entry (invariant 9) — the header's own settlement is then 'mixed', a value the task spec's own contract did not list (reported, the identical correction T-170's credit_basis needed).

title: customer.credit-applied — spending it against a later trade order
text:
The credit drawn down inside ar_collection's own posting (recordCollection's creditApplied extension, the AR mirror of T-130 §5), not a separate document type. A ₱600 order paid ENTIRELY from an existing ₱600 credit — no cash moves.
2140 Customer store credits payable - 600.00 - customer
1210 Accounts receivable - 600.00 - customer
Trap: the money-account leg of ar_collection is a zero-amount line here and is OMITTED — moneyAccountId is still named on the collection record even though no draw happens against it. Built by extending recordCollection, never a bare journal entry — bypassing the real AR subledger (ar_collections/ar_collection_allocations) would drift openItems from the raw ledger, the exact 13.3% class of bug repo/ar.ts's own header exists to prevent.

title: customer.return-internal — a branch returning to its own commissary, T-173 backwards
text:
A branch returns ₱400 of prepped goods to the commissary that shipped them.
2150 Due to related store - branch - 400.00 - store
1310 Inventory - branch - 400.00
1310 Inventory - commissary - 400.00
1250 Due from related store - commissary - 400.00 - store
Trap: asserted by absence in the real test — the tempting implementation treats every return the same way and adds a 4950, 2140/refund leg here too. No revenue, no contra-revenue, no credit, no refund — a branch has no credit relationship with its own commissary (ADR-008 §8, the same derived-treatment fact that decides a dispatch, T-133 §5). There is no margin to carry on a straight return (unlike T-133's dispatch): the value moves at exactly what the branch's own layer was valued at, never a fresh cost, never the day's price list.
---

title: Franchise dispatch (trade_order_dispatch, inter-entity) — v2-only, T-398 S5, ADR-008 §4
text:
The commissary sells to a franchise that is another company in its own organisation (Padre Garcia). Nothing eliminates: the commissary recognises revenue and cost, the franchise recognises stock and a payable, each in its own organisation and its own transaction. No entry ever has lines in two organisations. The two sides are tied by the shipment note (inter_entity_shipments) and checked by the daily reconciliation, never by a shared transaction.
VAT: pending Q5 (Ian answers by 13 Nov). v2 computes no VAT (bible #75). Every amount below is the VAT-inclusive price as billed. A line marked FENCED is one whose amount, or whose existence, changes if Q5's final answer is (a) "VAT-registered, prices inclusive": revenue and inventory would then post net of VAT, with the VAT on 2250 VAT payable (seller; reserved today) and an input-VAT asset (buyer; no account yet). If Q5 is (b), nothing here changes. No test may assert that a VAT line is absent.
One worked order for every pattern: 10.000 kg pork belly (raw_material, so 1310) at ₱310.00/kg = ₱3,100.00, FIFO cost ₱250.00/kg = ₱2,500.00. The order carries no delivery fee (QO-6) and no pay-now (row 370).

title: trade_dispatch.franchise — seller, at dispatch: a real sale, identical to an outside buyer's
text:
Posted in the commissary's organisation, store = the commissary, dated the order's date. In code these are TWO entries — the sale by recordCharge (source_type = 'trade_order_dispatch', the AR charge) and the cost by postConsumption (source_id = <order>:1310) — shown together, as customer.return-ar is.
1210 Accounts receivable - 3,100.00 - customer (Padre Garcia)
4300 Wholesale sales — FENCED (Q5) - 3,100.00
5100 COGS — food - 2,500.00
1310 Inventory — raw materials - 2,500.00
*2250 VAT payable — FENCED (Q5), not posted* - *—*
Trap: the legs are byte-identical to an external sale of the same lines (leg E1 compares against a control order). The franchise branch adds no ledger line: what it adds is the shipment row, written in the same transaction. Never the 1340, 1250, 2150 internal shape: that eliminates, and between two companies nothing eliminates. customer_group = 'franchise' decides nothing; only customers.counterparty_org_id does (ADR-008 §2). The credit limit gate inside recordCharge applies as for any customer (E27).

title: trade_receipt.franchise — buyer, at PG's receipt: the stock arrives
text:
Posted in Padre Garcia's organisation by PG's receive_delivery holder, store = PG's store, dated the receipt date, through the existing receiveDelivery → postReceiptValue (source_type = 'stock_receipt'). The unit cost of the new FIFO layer is the shipment's rate (₱310.00), never the commissary's cost, which PG cannot see.
1310 Inventory — raw materials — FENCED (Q5) - 3,100.00
2120 Goods received not invoiced - 3,100.00
*input VAT asset — FENCED (Q5), no account yet, not posted* - *—*
Trap: valued at what PG received × the shipment rate, never at the dispatched quantity (mutant: post at the dispatched quantity → E7 red). Over-receipt is refused (received ≤ shipped per line, E20): an extra the commissary did not bill is not PG's stock to book at a price nobody set.

title: trade_receipt.franchise-bill — buyer, same transaction: the shipment is the bill
text:
The shipment note is the commissary's bill, so PG's receipt also writes a system supplier bill for exactly the received value and clears 2120 to 2110 (source_type = 'stock_receipt_invoice', linkInvoiceToReceipt, variance zero by construction). This is what gives PG an open AP item it can pay from its ordinary AP payment screen.
2120 Goods received not invoiced - 3,100.00
2110 Accounts payable - 3,100.00 - supplier (the commissary, suppliers.counterparty_org_id = Ian's org)
Trap: no 5450 line can arise (the bill equals the receipt to the centavo); one appearing means the receipt and the bill were valued differently — a defect, not a variance. Never 2110 without the bill row: ap.openItems reads bills, so a bare 2110 credit would be a debt PG can see but never pay.

title: trade_dispatch.franchise_transit_shortage — seller, after reconciliation: the credit note
text:
PG received 8.000 of 10.000 kg, so PG owes ₱2,480.00 (its two entries above at ₱2,480.00). The 06:30 reconciliation raises one franchise_credit discrepancy in the commissary's organisation; the commissary manager posts this credit note, in the commissary's organisation, store = the commissary (A7). PG posts nothing — its payable is already for what it received.
4950 Sales returns and voids — FENCED (Q5) - 620.00
1210 Accounts receivable - 620.00 - customer (Padre Garcia)
5300 Wastage and spoilage - 500.00
5100 COGS — food - 500.00

title: Cash request release and return (cash_request_release 82 legs / cash_request_return 52 legs)
text:
The pair, together. In v1, 1120 (staff-custodian cash) is not a requires_party account — a plain asset, not a control account with a subledger.
v2 DIFFERS HERE, deliberately (T-144, bible row 159). Not because v1 loses the holder — it names them on the request document. Because the LEDGER cannot decompose 1120 without that document: one staff-float account per store, two people able to hold floats at once, so the account alone is a single balance. v1 answers *"how much is still out?"* with a stored remainingAmount for exactly this reason. In v2 the leg carries party_type = 'cash_request', party_id = the request. The legs below are otherwise unchanged; only the party is added.

title: cash_request.release — A float handed to a staff custodian
text:
A ₱2,000 cash float is released from the cashier drawer for a market run. The operational request itself has no GL effect at all (bible §16.10) — only the release does.
1120 Cash on hand — staff custodian - 2,000.00 - cash_request
1110 Cash on hand — cashier - 2,000.00 - —

title: cash_request.return — The unused float comes back
text:
Of the ₱2,000 float, ₱350 is unspent and returned.
1110 Cash on hand — cashier - 350.00 - —
1120 Cash on hand — staff custodian - 350.00 - cash_request

title: Commissary dispatch (commissary_dispatch) — 70 legs, the inter-store elimination case
text:
For a franchise (another company), see Franchise dispatch below: a real sale on both sides, never this elimination.
No v1 leg-mapping entry exists for this shape (v1's commissary_receive sourceType is dead at the financial layer and name-collides with a live inventory-ledger type of the same string — COA-ALIGNMENT §2 "Retire" table). This is a genuine v2 design, built from the reciprocal-account pattern COA-ALIGNMENT §2 already specifies for due-from/due-to. Bible landmine #27's fix ("one real ACID transaction; both stores are rows in one database") makes this one journal entry spanning two stores, not v1's "fake distributed transaction" (two best-effort writes). Phase 3 owns valuation (weighted average, real stock movement); this pattern owns the shape only.

title: commissary_dispatch.transfer — HISTORICAL, periodic era only (until 2026-09-02, T-165)
text:
RETIRED 2026-09-02 — T-165, the switch. Nothing posts this shape any more; kept for anyone reading an entry dated before the switch. The live pattern is the perpetual, two-event shape below. CORRECTED 2026-08-28, T-133. This pattern used to move 1330 inventory between the two stores, which assumes perpetual inventory — and this system was, at the time, periodic. Verified rather than assumed: every expense category mapped to a 5xxx COGS account (seed/expense-categories.ts — Meat → 5110), there was no capitalisation path anywhere, and nothing in the codebase debited 1310, 1330 or 1340. The inventory shape drove the seller's 1330 negative and left the cost stranded in the seller's P&L, so the receiving branch could not expense what it received at all. Found by Ian asking how Malvar expenses a slab Lipa processed.
₱31,000 of prepped goods ships from the Malvar commissary to the Lipa branch: a 100 kg slab bought at ₱300/kg and processed at ₱10/kg. The transfer price is what carries the processing cost — ₱310, not ₱300. That is the mechanism by which the seller's work reaches the buyer's books.
5175 Cost transferred to branches - commissary - 31,000.00 - —

title: commissary.discrepancy-charge — the same gap, recovered instead of written off
text:
1230 Advances to employees - commissary - 3,000.00 - employee
1340 Inventory in transit - commissary - 3,000.00 - —
This is an ASSET, not an expense. 1230 is a receivable from the named staffer, drawn down by a payroll deduction, and its line carries the PERSON as party_type = 'employee'.
Nothing in the codebase credits 1230 yet — . The charge is still offered rather than blocked, because refusing it would force a genuinely recoverable shortfall to be written off as a loss instead — worse, and irreversible in the books.

title: commissary.discrepancy-extra-dispatch — an over-receipt the commissary confirms it really sent
text:
The branch counted one more than was dispatched; the receipt booked only what was sent and the extra became an over discrepancy. When the commissary manager confirms it did send it, the extra is booked at both stores in one entry (rate ₱500, one unit, ₱300 layer cost).
1310 Inventory — raw materials - branch - 500.00 - —
2150 Due to related store - branch - 500.00 - store
1250 Due from related store - commissary - 500.00 - store
1310 Inventory — raw materials - commissary - 300.00 - —
5175 Cost transferred to branches - commissary - 200.00 - —
No 1340 leg. These goods were never put into transit on the books; dispatch and receipt collapse into one event, so a 1340 debit and credit would net to zero and only add noise.
The commissary's credit is what consume() relieved (layer cost), not the line's rate. Dispatch itself relieves at layer cost, so any other figure makes the commissary's stock ledger and 1310 disagree; the branch's side is at the rate, as the receipt is. The margin is Cr 5175 when positive and Dr 5175 when the rate is below cost; zero-value legs are omitted.

title: The dispositions that post NOTHING
text:
audit posts nothing and does not clear the day-open block. It records that a human looked and chose to wait, and the row stays open. An escape hatch that cleared the block would be a way to make a dispute disappear without deciding it, which is the state the whole task exists to prevent.
late_receipt posts nothing here either — the rest turned up, and T-173's second confirm posts the balance itself. Posting here as well would relieve 1340 twice for one lot of goods.
return posts nothing, and that is correct. It resolves an over-receipt that went back to the commissary or was only a miscount (a note is required, saying who carried it back and when, or that the branch recounted). A receipt books at most what was dispatched, so the excess was never on the branch's books; a reversing entry would take the branch below what it really holds. The resolved row itself is the record.
An over-receipt books the dispatched quantity, and its receipt entry is byte-identical to a full receipt: the cap leaves the receipt legs exactly as a full receipt writes them, and the excess waits as an over discrepancy (blocking day-open like a shortage) until a manager decides.

title: commissary.receipt-freight — outbound freight on an internal order, charged to the branch
text:
An internal order from the commissary to a branch carries a ₱1,000 delivery fee and ₱200 of other fees (trade_orders.delivery_fee + other_fees): ₱1,200 is what the truck cost. It posts at receipt, in the receipt's transaction, as its own entry beside the goods entry (postInternalFreight, T-372/), dated the day the branch received.
6630 Vehicle and transportation - branch - 1,200.00 - —
2150 Due to related store - branch - 1,200.00 - store
1250 Due from related store - commissary - 1,200.00 - store
6630 Vehicle and transportation - commissary - 1,200.00 - —
The branch bears the haulage (Ian's ruling Q1 (a), 2026-09-30): the debit is the branch's own 6630, and the branch owes the commissary for it through the same 2150, 1250 reciprocal pair the goods entry uses. The commissary's 6630 credit recovers what it already spent on the trip through its own expenses, so consolidated the two 6630 legs net to zero — the same elimination 5175 performs for the goods margin. Each store's own lines net to zero on their own.

title: Channel settlement (channel_settlement) — T-150, the thing that clears 1220
text:
T-123 raises 1220 Channel receivable on every verified Foodpanda / Grab day, and until T-150 nothing had ever cleared it — the balance only grew. This is 74% of v1's AR collection volume.
1220 and the clearing accounts do different jobs, and collapsing them loses an alarm:
1220 Channel receivable, party = channel - *"Foodpanda owes us ₱X, and it is 12 days old."*
1221 / 1222 Channel clearing - *"Something did not finish."* — zero at rest
The trap, restated because it cost ₱198,148.29 once: these fees are booked here, once. A module that posts this settlement *and* lets someone raise a separate expense document for the same platform fee has rebuilt the confirmed v1 defect (see channel_settlement.plain below).

title: channel_settlement.plain — fees to real accounts, receivable to exactly zero
text:
A ₱100,000 Foodpanda day: ₱20,000 commission, ₱500 withheld at source, ₱79,500 banked.
1140 E-wallet / online channels - 79,500.00 - money_account
6400 Platform and channel fees - 20,000.00 - —
6800 Taxes and licences - 500.00 - —
1220 Channel receivable - 100,000.00 - channel
Trap: the withheld tax is an expense, not an asset. RR 2-98 §2.58.3(B) allows a creditable withholding tax to be claimed only when the income payment has been declared as part of gross income with the 2307 attached; bible §13 row 75 records that reported sales are not all sales and that this ledger is never a filing basis. The credit cannot be realised, so there is no future benefit and therefore no asset. Do not seed a 1270 creditable-withholding asset — an account that exists invites someone to use it.
The destination account is per-channel CONFIG, not a constant: 1140 requires a money_account party and 1130 Cash on hand — office does not, so the posting asks the chart rather than hard-coding either.

title: channel_settlement.promo_credit — a NEGATIVE deduction, which is a real credit
text:
A ₱50,000 day where the platform charged ₱8,000 commission and handed back ₱1,000 of promo funding.
1140 E-wallet / online channels - 43,000.00 - money_account
6400 Platform and channel fees - 8,000.00 - —
6400 Platform and channel fees - 1,000.00 - —
1220 Channel receivable - 50,000.00 - channel
Trap: a deduction is SIGNED and nothing may clamp it to zero. A promo-heavy day genuinely returns money, and v1 shipped a bug by assuming a deduction is always positive. The credit leg is the whole point of this fixture.

title: channel_settlement.loan_two_legs — two loans docked from one payout, one of them another store's
text:
A ₱10,000 Grab day for the Lipa branch: ₱2,500 commission, and Grab docks two loans out of the payout — ₱590 on a Lipa loan and ₱1,770 on a loan owned by the commissary. ₱5,140 is banked. One leg per loan, posted in the order given (T-511 S6a).
1140 E-wallet / online channels - 5,140.00 - money_account
6400 Platform and channel fees - 2,500.00 - —
2400 Loans payable (Lipa branch) - 590.00 - loan
1250 Due from related store (Lipa branch) - 1,770.00 - store
2400 Loans payable (commissary) - 1,770.00 - loan
2150 Due to related store (commissary) - 1,770.00 - store
1220 Channel receivable (Lipa branch) - 10,000.00 - channel
Trap: the loan deduction is the sum of the legs, and the database holds the two equal at commit, so a leg is never a lump. A leg whose loan belongs to another store is the 1250 / 2400 / 2150 triple, not a bare 2400: the paying store gave up cash that was not its debt, so it is owed (1250); the owning store's loan falls (2400) and it now owes the paying store (2150). Invariant 6's reciprocal check proves 1250 = 2150 across stores. Two legs of the same loan and owner store are refused — put the amounts together.

title: channel_settlement.shortfall_acknowledged — a shortfall past tolerance, accepted by a person with a reason
text:
A ₱10,000 Grab day with ₱2,500 commission and only ₱4,000 banked: ₱3,500 short, far past the ₱1,000 tolerance. A manager checks the statement, agrees the day was over-reported and types why. The reason is stored on the settlement (T-511 S6a).
1140 E-wallet / online channels - 4,000.00 - money_account
6400 Platform and channel fees - 2,500.00 - —
6420 Channel settlement variance - 3,500.00 - —
1220 Channel receivable - 10,000.00 - channel
Trap: past tolerance, a difference of either sign needs a person's acknowledgement with a reason: a shortfall books to 6420 (expense), a gain to 7100 (income), never the other way round and never silently. Within tolerance nothing is asked and nothing is stored. The receivable clears exactly either way.

title: channel_settlement.nets_period_charge — the payout already netted a booked period charge, so it is not expensed again
text:
The weekly charge of channel_charge.period_fee below (₱100 fee + ₱12 VAT = ₱112) is booked, and another day is still owed. Foodpanda pays a ₱10,000 day, takes ₱2,000 of day fees (VAT included) and the ₱112 charge: ₱7,888 is banked. The settlement names the charge it nets (settleChargeIds, T-511 S6c).
1140 E-wallet / online channels - 7,888.00 - money_account
6400 Platform and channel fees - 2,000.00 - —
1220 Channel receivable - 9,888.00 - channel
Trap: the platform takes a charge you already booked, so the payout is SHORT of the day by exactly that charge. Settled the plain way, that gap (112) is swept to 6420 and the charge is expensed twice (6400 112 and 6420 112); at the default tolerance it books silently. Naming the charge credits 1220 by the day LESS the charge (9,888, which is also the stored outstanding_cleared), so the difference is zero. A charge counts as netted only while its settlement stands: a void frees it. The tolerance never decides this; the link does.

title: channel_settlement.grab_day_after_correction — approve a Grab day: the platform figure replaces the staff figure first (T-511 S7a)
text:
Staff typed a ₱10,000 Grab day (Dr 1220 / Cr 4150 ₱10,000). The Grab file says ₱11,000, with ₱2,200 commission, a ₱100 platform fee, a ₱500 loan repayment and ₱8,200 paid out. approveDay posts two entries in ONE transaction. First the correction (sale.platform-correction): Dr 1220 ₱1,000 (party the channel) / Cr 4150 ₱1,000, dated on the sales day. Then the settlement:
1140 E-wallet / online channels - 8,200.00 - money_account
6400 Platform and channel fees - 2,200.00 - —
6400 Platform and channel fees - 100.00 - —
2400 Loans payable - 500.00 - loan
1220 Channel receivable - 11,000.00 - channel
The difference is zero, so nothing is asked of the approver and nothing is swept. The settlement posts commission and platform fee as two 6400 lines (₱2,300 in all).

title: channel_settlement.foodpanda_week_with_charge — approve a Foodpanda week: the last day nets the period charge once (T-511 S7a)
text:
One Foodpanda invoice covers three days: ₱9,000 (₱1,800 fees, ₱7,200 banked), ₱8,000 (₱1,600, ₱6,400) and ₱10,000 (₱2,000, ₱8,000 staged), plus a charge on no day: ₱100 and ₱12 VAT, ₱112, booked first by its own action (channel_charge.period_fee). The platform took the ₱112 out of the invoice payout, so the latest-dated day of the invoice is the carrier: it names the charge (settleChargeIds) and banks ₱8,000 less ₱112 = ₱7,888. The first two days approve as plain days.
1140 E-wallet / online channels - 7,888.00 - money_account
6400 Platform and channel fees - 2,000.00 - —
1220 Channel receivable - 9,888.00 - channel
The bank receives 7,200 + 6,400 + 7,888 = ₱21,488.00, the invoice total, and 6400 holds the charge once (112) plus the day fees.
Trap: only ONE day carries the charge. Name it on an earlier day and that day banks less than it should while the carrier banks too much; name it nowhere and the ₱112 is swept to 6420 and expensed twice. The carrier is held (period_charge_unbooked) until the charge is booked. If the carrier day is rejected the charge stays a credit on 1220, and a void of the carrier frees the charge so the re-approve nets it again.
---

title: Platform period charge (channel_charge) — v2-only, T-511 S6c
text: A delivery platform's weekly fee (and any uncategorised Appendix B charge) belongs to no sales day, so no settlement books it. postPlatformCharge books it once from the staged line and its stored VAT, dated on the charge when its month is open, else today (Ian, 15 Nov: a late charge or credit note never goes into a closed month). Owner decision (BOSS, 7 Nov): new source type channel_charge.

title: channel_charge.period_fee — a platform charge with no sales day, fee and VAT as one expense
text:
A Foodpanda invoice carries a ₱100 weekly platform fee that no sales day can pay, and ₱12 of VAT on it.
6400 Platform and channel fees - 112.00 - —
1220 Channel receivable - 112.00 - channel
Trap: the VAT is part of the cost (no VAT engine, no input-VAT account: bible row 75), so ONE 6400 line carries fee plus VAT. The credit goes to 1220 with the channel as party, or the platform aging and the settlement cannot see it. A platform credit note is the same two accounts on the opposite sides, never a negative amount. The posting is recorded once per staged line, so approving the same invoice twice books it once, and the payout that later takes it must say so (channel_settlement.nets_period_charge).
---

title: Channel receivable move (channel_receivable_reclass) — v2-only, T-606
text: A delivery-platform channel (Grab, Foodpanda) must use 1220 Channel receivable, because settlements, platform files, period charges and the platform aging all read only that account. Lipa's two channels were set to 1210 Accounts receivable (the customer account) and about 40 verified days sit there. An admin presses "Move to Channel receivable" on the channel's card (moveChannelToChannelReceivable): one transaction locks the channel, moves what it holds per store, and switches the setting. Dated today (Manila) when today's month is open; if it is closed, nothing is changed and the admin is told. Ian, 18 Nov: "move the foodpanda and grab sales directly".

title: channel_receivable.reclass — a platform channel's balance moves from 1210 to 1220
text:
Lipa Foodpanda is owed ₱12,345.00 and its days were posted on 1210.
1220 Channel receivable - 12,345.00 - channel
1210 Accounts receivable - 12,345.00 - channel
Trap: both lines carry the channel as party and the store the balance sits at, one pair per store. A net credit balance posts the opposite sides, never a negative amount. The old day entries are not touched: they stay on 1210 for ever, so a later platform-file correction reads what was posted for the day by party, not by account. A zero balance posts nothing and only switches the setting. The button also shows for a channel already on 1220 while a balance sits on another account (the move entry was reversed, an old day voided): that press sweeps it with the same entry. Each press has its own request id, so a replay of the same press posts nothing; with nothing left a press does nothing.
---

text: Always both legs, same shape as depreciation. One of ADR-005's five January-required capabilities.

title: amortization.monthly — Monthly amortisation of a prepaid item
text:
A ₱1,100 monthly slice of a prepaid insurance policy is recognised as expense.
6750 Amortisation - 1,100.00 - —
1400 Prepaid expenses - 1,100.00 - —

title: Production / conversion (production_conversion) — v2-only, T-176
text: A slicing run or a prep batch posts as ONE stock transaction: inputs out, outputs in, cost carried across — a conversion, not a purchase or a sale.

title: production.conversion.slice — a slab becomes three sliced products, plus a yield loss
text:
100 kg of slab bought at ₱300/kg is cut into 97 kg of three sliced products, with ₱1,000 of labour attached. The 3 kg gap is real trim loss, valued at the input's own rate.
1310 Inventory — raw materials (output value, sliced meat) - 30,100.00 - —
5300 Wastage and spoilage (the yield gap's value) - 900.00 - —
1310 Inventory — raw materials (slab relief) - 30,000.00 - —
6100 Salaries and wages (labour capitalised into cost) - 1,000.00 - —
Trap: the task spec's own worked example books the output to 1330; this implementation books it to 1310 instead, because the output item's kind stays meat_sliced (its own parent_slab_item_id contract demands it) and meat_sliced already maps to 1310 in the one existing account router (INVENTORY_ACCOUNT_BY_ITEM_KIND) — reusing it rather than hardcoding a second one. See docs/DEFECTS-REGISTER.md /. Do not port v1's memo-only yield-loss leg forward — it is a real cost here.

title: Wastage (wastage_expense) — 16 legs
text: v2 wastage debits 5300 and credits inventory directly — COA-ALIGNMENT §2's "Retire" table explicitly retires v1's net-zero memo-pair (incomewastage_writeoff_contra): "a real economic entry, no memo needed."

title: wastage_expense.spoilage — A real cost of sales, straight against inventory
text:
₱640 of spoiled pork belly is written off. Moved from OPEX to cost of sales per COA-ALIGNMENT §1 rule 5 — the standard treatment, and it will make reported gross margin more correct, not more flattering.
5300 Wastage and spoilage - 640.00 - —
1310 Inventory — raw materials - 640.00 - —
Trap: do not port v1's net-zero contra-memo pair forward — this is a real, single economic entry: an expense against an asset, not an expense against an income-side memo that cancels itself out.
---

title: Order/channel wastage (order_wastage) — v2-only, T-178
text: A refunded or remade channel order. NOT stock wastage (see wastage_expense above) — no stock movement, no layer. 1220 is the credit in every case that posts; platform_paid posts nothing.

title: wastage.order-absorbed — the store eats a ₱150 Foodpanda refund
text:
5300 Wastage and spoilage - 150.00 - —
1220 Channel receivable - 150.00 - channel

title: wastage.order-charged — split 60/40 between two staff
text:
1230 Advances to employees - 60.00 - employee (staff A)
1230 Advances to employees - 40.00 - employee (staff B)
1220 Channel receivable - 100.00 - channel
Gated on Phase 5 (staff advances) — refused today; isPhase5StaffAdvancesAvailable() in packages/domain/src/wastage/orders.ts is the one flag. platform_paid posts nothing — T-150's settlement already cleared 1220 for the day (proved not to double-clear against it, end to end, in order-wastage.test.ts).

title: Remittance (remittance) — 10 legs
text: Cash-cashier OUT + cash-office IN, always. Then either 1230 IN (shortage, not P&L) or 7350 IN (overage, P&L) — never both, and neither when expected equals actual. Bible §16.6: fee and variance accounts "net as a signed total... never clamp at zero" — the same discipline applies to 7350.

title: remittance.exact — The conditional leg genuinely absent
text:
The cashier remits ₱12,000, and expected and counted match exactly. Two legs only.
1130 Cash on hand — office - 12,000.00 - —
1110 Cash on hand — cashier - 12,000.00 - —

title: remittance.overage — 7350 swings positive
text:
Expected ₱10,000, actually counted ₱10,080 — ₱80 more than the books say should be there.
Two entries, not one (T-366 S3; Ian, 2026-09-30, A1 Q3: a manager confirms an overage before it becomes income). Between the handover and the confirmation, 1110 carries the ₱80 as a credit and 7350 is untouched — that state is expected, not an error.
1 · At handover (the transfer; the overage is recorded as an open variance):
1130 Cash on hand — office - 10,080.00 - —
1110 Cash on hand — cashier - 10,080.00 - —
2 · When a manager confirms (resolveRemittanceVariance, action recognise_income; key remittance-variance:<id>:income, sourceType remittance_variance, excluded from the day's owed):
1110 Cash on hand — cashier (or the R5 from-account; 1140 carries its party) - 80.00 - —
7350 Cash over and short - 80.00 - —
Net of both: Dr 1130 10,080 · Cr 1110 10,000 · Cr 7350 80. Reversing the handover reverses entry 2 too.

title: remittance.shortage — Charged to the responsible cashier, not P&L
text:
Expected ₱10,000, only ₱9,850 counted — a ₱150 shortage, charged to the cashier.
1130 Cash on hand — office - 9,850.00 - —
1230 Advances to employees - 150.00 - employee
1110 Cash on hand — cashier - 10,000.00 - —
Trap: 7350 is one account that swings either way — never a separate account per direction. A shortage does not touch 7350 at all; it goes to 1230, not P&L.
In v2 this is two entries, and the net is identical (T-366 S2, ). The handover posts the transfer of what was counted (Dr 1130 9,850 / Cr 1110 9,850, remittance). Charging the shortage is a second entry when a manager resolves the variance: Dr 1230 150.00 (party employee) / Cr 1110 150.00, source_type 'remittance_variance', linked from remittance_variances.journal_entry_id (the database refuses a charged variance without one). Together they equal the table above. Charging from a wallet credits 1140 instead, with party money_account = that wallet. Reversing the remittance reverses both.
---

title: Balance adjustment (balance_adjustment) — 10 legs — THE ANTI-PATTERN
text: Required, and explicitly marked as the pattern to design out. v1's real sourceType for what T-113 called "liability-charge".

title: balance_adjustment.plug — Included so nobody ports it forward
text:
An SSS payable balance is found ₱850 too low after a manual reconciliation. Instead of finding and reversing the entry that got it wrong, someone plugs the difference directly.
6110 Employer SSS contributions - 850.00 - —
2210 SSS payable - 850.00 - —
Trap: THIS IS THE PATTERN TO DESIGN OUT. v2 should make it unnecessary: a correction is a reversal with a reason (T-106), not an adjusting line that references nothing. This fixture exists to be pointed at, not copied — if a Phase 2 module reaches for this shape to "fix" a wrong balance, the right move is reverseEntry on the entry that was actually wrong, not a plug like this one.

title: Statutory remittance (liability_payment)
text: "Cash OUT + liability OUT. Pure balance sheet." Not in the v1 frequency table by leg count, but ADR-005's scope-gap section names "generic liability accounts" as one of five capabilities that cannot wait past January. Doubles as bible §16.5's worked "remit to agency" example.

title: liability_payment.statutory-remittance — Settling what was withheld, not new expense
text:
₱5,000 of withheld SSS contributions is actually remitted to the agency. Bible §16.5: "if you never remit, the liability sits there and grows — that is the feature, not a gap." This is the remit step, distinct from withholding it and from the employer share, both already booked earlier at payroll time.
2210 SSS payable - 5,000.00 - —
1110 Cash on hand — cashier - 5,000.00 - —
Trap: this is not a new expense — the expense (employer share) and the withholding (employee share) were already recognised when payroll posted. Posting this again as an expense would double the true statutory cost — the same shape of bug as the AR platform-fee double-count above.

title: Statutory payment (statutory_payment)
text:
T-193. Paying SSS, PhilHealth, Pag-IBIG or BIR the contributions payroll already set aside in 2210-2240. One entry per payment; the form's own request id is the document id and the idempotency key is statutory_payment:{id}:post. Not liability_payment: reverseLiabilityEntry accepts that source type, and a statutory payment is undone only by its own void. The older liability_payment.statutory-remittance example above stays as bible §16.5's illustration.
The cost was booked when payroll posted, so no leg here ever touches 6100-6130 (the §16.7 double count). Only the money account's credit carries a party, and only when it is 1140 (party money_account); a staff float (1120) is refused by name. The ₱3,180.00 below is one store's SSS for one month (employee, employer and EC shares together).

title: statutory_payment.same-store - One store pays its own SSS from its own safe
text:
Lipa pays its October SSS, ₱3,180.00, out of Lipa's office safe.
2210 SSS payable - Lipa - 3,180.00 - -
1130 Cash on hand - office - Lipa - 3,180.00 - -
Trap: this is not an expense. Debiting 6110 SSS expense here counts the same contribution twice and leaves 2210 at ₱3,180.00 for ever.

title: statutory_payment.cross-store - One store's SSS paid from another store's safe
text:
The same ₱3,180.00, owed at Lipa, paid out of Malvar's office safe. The safe's credit sits at the safe's store, the debt is discharged at Lipa, and the pair between the stores records who now owes whom. One payment naming three stores gets one such pair per store paid for.
2210 SSS payable - Lipa - 3,180.00 - -
2150 Due to related store - Lipa - 3,180.00 - store (Malvar)
1250 Due from related store - Malvar - 3,180.00 - store (Lipa)
1130 Cash on hand - office - Malvar - 3,180.00 - -
Trap: debiting 2210 at the paying store balances perfectly and is wrong: Lipa's SSS payable never falls and Malvar's goes negative (the shape). The pair's party is the other store's code, not its id.

title: statutory_payment.with-penalty - Late, with the agency's surcharge
text:
The same ₱3,180.00 paid on 15 December with a ₱63.60 surcharge from the agency. The surcharge is a new cost of its own: it goes to 6810 at the paying store, never into 2210 (which would push the payable below what payroll owed) and never into 6110.
2210 SSS payable - Lipa - 3,180.00 - -
6810 Penalties and surcharges - Lipa - 63.60 - -
1130 Cash on hand - office - Lipa - 3,243.60 - -
Trap: adding the surcharge to the 2210 line makes the payment look like it settled ₱3,243.60 of contributions, so the month shows overpaid, and the surcharge never reaches the profit and loss statement.

title: Owner equity movements (capital_contribution / drawing)
text: Not in T-108's own v1-leg-count frequency table (too rare in the historical corpus), but ADR-005's scope-gap section names "owner equity movements" explicitly as one of five capabilities v1 already posts that cannot wait past January, and bible §16.10's minimum pattern list names "owner drawings" by name. COA-ALIGNMENT §4.7 #2: drawings were never used in v1 — this is an add, not a correct, designed right from the start rather than migrating a broken pattern.

title: equity.capital_contribution — Cash in, equity grows
text:
The owner injects ₱100,000 of fresh capital into the business.
1110 Cash on hand — cashier - 100,000.00 - —
3100 Owner's capital - 100,000.00 - —

title: equity.drawing — Reduces equity, on the books at last
text:
The owner withdraws ₱25,000 for personal use. 3200 is debit-normal (contra-equity) — one of the six accounts across the whole chart that breaks derive-from-type, alongside 1590 and the four contra-revenue accounts.
3200 Owner's drawings - 25,000.00 - —
1110 Cash on hand — cashier - 25,000.00 - —
Trap: 3200 is type='equity' but normal_balance='debit'. A drawing debits 3200 to increase it (reduce equity) — the same mechanic as accumulated depreciation debiting-to-increase on the asset side. Do not assume every equity account credits to increase.

title: Year close (year_close) — v2-only, ADR-006
text: Every income and expense balance for the year zeroes into 3300 Retained earnings, posted through the same postEntry every other entry uses, dated the first day of the following year, carrying source_type = 'year_close' so a date-range P&L can exclude it while a balance-sheet-as-of includes it.

title: Opening balance (opening_balance) — v2-only, ADR-005 (amended 2026-08-24) + bible row 106
text: One entry dated 2027-01-01, per-party lump sums for AR/AP, balancing to 3900. 3900 must net to exactly zero once loaded and reconciled — a residual halts, never gets plugged. This pair (load then reconcile) is the accounting judgement T-108 required: ADR-005 says 3900 must net to zero but does not spell out the two-step mechanism that makes that provable rather than definitionally true — see the T-108 task report.

title: opening_balance.load — The 2027-01-01 load, balance-sheet only, per-party lump sums
text:
The closed, adjusted trial balance from the old ERP as at 2026-12-31, loaded as one entry dated 2027-01-01. AR and AP are one lump sum per party (Ian: *"we will lump-sum their balances per vendor... date all AR and AP January 1 and start from there"*) — no per-invoice detail is migrated; that lives in the spreadsheet, deliberately. Every other balance-sheet account books against 3900, the temporary clearing account this whole load nets through.
1110 Cash on hand — cashier - 80,000.00 - —
1210 Accounts receivable - 15,000.00 - customer
1510 Property and equipment - 300,000.00 - —
1590 Accumulated depreciation - 40,000.00 - —
2110 Accounts payable - 22,000.00 - supplier
3900 Opening balance equity - 333,000.00 - —
Trap: v2 assumes a zero starting point everywhere else (bible row 106) — this is the one exception, and only for balance-sheet positions, never for history. Nothing here is a replay of 2026 transactions; it is a snapshot of where things stood on 31 December. AR and AP open as one balance per party — the opening lump is always dated first, so it is always oldest and payments draw it down before any 2027 invoice.

title: Reversal — the correction path (T-106)
text:
Not its own business event; the mechanism every pattern above shares. Every single fixture in this document has been posted, then reversed, through the real reverseEntry, and proved to net to exactly zero per account (tests/integration/posting-patterns.test.ts's own "(reversal)" pass). A posted entry is never edited — a correction is a new, dated, opposite entry (reverseEntry), never a quiet change to history.
Two things a Phase 2 module must get right, proved here for the hardest cases (control accounts, inter-store, opening balance, year close):
1. Party travels with the reversal. A line on a requires_party control account (AP, AR, a staff advance, a loan, an inter-store due-from/due-to) reverses with the same party — only debit and credit swap. found this did not work at all until this task's own fix (see the T-108 task report). 2. A closed-period original needs an explicit reversalDate in an open period, and the reversal's memo is prefixed [prior period] — T-106's own contract, unchanged by this task.
